name: Sun
visual_anchor: Blazing golden solar orb radiating coronal flares and prominences against the dark black void of deep space.
core_traits: Center star of our solar system comprising 99.86% of its entire total mass
Yellow dwarf (G-type main-sequence star) fueled by thermonuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium
Surface temperature around 5,500°C with core temperatures exceeding 15 million °C
Light takes roughly 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth

facts_and_myths.claim: The Sun is an enormous raging ball of burning fire and flames.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Sun does not burn via chemical fire (combustion); it generates energy through nuclear fusion turning hydrogen into helium.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Roughly 600 million tons of hydrogen are converted into helium every single second in its core.

facts_and_myths.claim: Over one million Earths could fit inside the volume of the Sun.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With a diameter 109 times larger than Earth, approximately 1.3 million Earths would fit inside a hollow Sun.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Sun is about 4.6 billion years old and roughly halfway through its lifespan.

name: Moon
visual_anchor: Glowing silver full moon displaying detailed cratered maria against a starry midnight sky.
core_traits: Earth's only natural permanent satellite
Fifth-largest natural satellite in the solar system
Tidally locked with Earth, meaning the same face always points toward us
Gravitational pull drives ocean tides on Earth

facts_and_myths.claim: The Moon has a permanent 'dark side' that never receives any sunlight at all.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The far side receives as much sunlight as the near side; it is only dark from Earth's perspective because it is tidally locked.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The first photographs of the Moon's far side were taken by Soviet Luna 3 probe in 1959.

facts_and_myths.claim: Footprints left by Apollo astronauts on the Moon could remain preserved for millions of years.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because the Moon has no atmosphere, wind, or liquid water erosion, footprints will only fade from micrometeorite impacts.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin stepped onto lunar soil on July 20, 1969.

name: Mars
visual_anchor: Crimson sphere of Mars showing dusty polar ice caps and the massive gash of Valles Marineris canyon.
core_traits: Fourth planet from the Sun in the solar system
Nicknamed the Red Planet due to ubiquitous iron oxide (rust) covering its surface
Home to Olympus Mons, the largest volcano and highest peak in the entire solar system
Possesses two small potato-shaped moons named Phobos and Deimos

facts_and_myths.claim: Sunsets on Mars appear distinctly blue rather than red or orange.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Fine martian iron dust scatters reddish light, allowing blue light to penetrate the thin atmosphere near the Sun's path.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: NASA rovers Curiosity and Perseverance have photographed breathtaking blue martian sunsets.

facts_and_myths.claim: Mars is roughly the same physical size as planet Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Mars is only about half the diameter of Earth and has just 11% of Earth's mass.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its gravity is roughly 38% of Earth's, so a 100 kg person would weigh just 38 kg on Mars.

name: Saturn
visual_anchor: Gas giant Saturn tilted gracefully with its brilliant concentric icy rings casting shadows across golden atmospheric bands.
core_traits: Sixth planet from the Sun and second largest in the solar system
Gas giant renowned for its spectacular, extensive ring system of ice particles and rock dust
Has more recognized moons than any other planet (over 140 moons)
Has a density lower than liquid water

facts_and_myths.claim: Saturn would float if placed in a colossal cosmic bathtub filled with water.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Saturn's mean density is about 0.687 g/cm³, which is significantly less dense than pure water (1 g/cm³).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It is the only planet in our solar system with an average density less than water.

facts_and_myths.claim: Saturn's rings are solid sheets of reflective ice metal.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The rings consist of billions of discrete particles ranging from microscopic ice specks to house-sized boulders.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The ring system spans 282,000 km across but is only about 10 meters thick in most places.

name: Mount Everest
visual_anchor: Pyramidal windswept peak of Mount Everest trailing a long white spindrift snow plume against deep sapphire blue sky.
core_traits: Highest mountain peak above sea level on Earth at 8,848.86 meters
Located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas on the Nepal-China border
First officially summitted by Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay in 1953
High altitude above 8,000 meters is known as the 'Death Zone'

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain from base to peak on planet Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: From underwater ocean base to summit, Hawaii's Mauna Kea measures over 10,200 meters, taller than Everest's elevation.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Everest is the highest mountain above sea level, but Mauna Kea is the tallest base-to-peak.

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Everest grows taller by roughly 4 millimeters every single year.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Continuous tectonic collision of the Indian and Eurasian continental plates pushes the Himalayas steadily upward.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Marine limestone fossils of ancient ocean creatures are found at the very top summit of Everest.

name: Mercury
visual_anchor: A heavily cratered, desolate grey planetary sphere silhouetted against the fierce blazing glare of the nearby Sun.
core_traits: Smallest planet in the solar system and closest to the Sun
Has no atmosphere, causing extreme temperature swings from 430 degrees Celsius by day to -180 degrees Celsius at night
Orbits the Sun in just 88 Earth days, faster than any other planet
Has a massive metallic iron core making up over 70% of its radius

facts_and_myths.claim: Mercury is the hottest planet in the solar system because it is closest to the Sun.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Venus is hotter than Mercury due to its runaway greenhouse effect trapping heat under dense clouds.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mercury experiences double sunrises in certain regions due to its eccentric elliptical orbit.

facts_and_myths.claim: A single day-night cycle on Mercury takes nearly two of its years.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Due to 3:2 spin-orbit resonance, one solar day on Mercury equals about 176 Earth days, while its year is 88 Earth days.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Despite scorching heat, radar observations found water ice hidden inside permanently shadowed polar craters.

name: Venus
visual_anchor: A glowing yellowish-white cloud-wrapped infernal planet spinning slowly amid a crushing superheated carbon dioxide atmosphere.
core_traits: Second planet from the Sun and the hottest planet in the solar system
Suffers from a runaway greenhouse effect maintaining surface temperatures of roughly 465 degrees Celsius
Surrounded by dense toxic clouds composed of sulfuric acid droplets
Rotates in the opposite direction (retrograde) compared to most other planets

facts_and_myths.claim: The Sun rises in the west and sets in the east on Venus.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because Venus spins backwards on its axis relative to its orbital motion, the Sun appears to rise in the west.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A day on Venus is longer than its year; it takes 243 Earth days to rotate once but only 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun.

facts_and_myths.claim: Soviet Venera spacecraft operated for days on the surface of Venus.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The extreme pressure (90 times Earth's) and melting temperatures crushed and melted probes within two hours.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Venera 13 survived the longest, lasting 127 minutes and sending back the first color photos of Venusian soil.

name: Earth
visual_anchor: A radiant blue and white marble world adorned with sapphire oceans, swirling cloud systems, and green continents suspended in dark space.
core_traits: Third planet from the Sun and the only known celestial body harboring life
Surface is roughly 71% liquid water, earning it the title Blue Planet
Possesses an oxygen-rich atmosphere and protective magnetic field driven by a liquid outer core
Has one large permanent natural satellite known as the Moon

facts_and_myths.claim: Earth is a perfect geometric sphere.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Earth is an oblate spheroid slightly flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator due to its rotational inertia.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Because of the equatorial bulge, Mount Chimborazo's summit is the closest place on Earth to the stars.

facts_and_myths.claim: Earth is the densest major planet in the solar system.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Earth has an average density of 5.51 grams per cubic centimeter, higher than all other planets including Jupiter.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Earth's magnetic pole drifts dozens of kilometers every single year.

name: Jupiter
visual_anchor: Colossal swirling banded gas giant planet dominated by the towering crimson eye of the Great Red Spot storm.
core_traits: Fifth planet from the Sun and the largest planet in our solar system
Massive gas giant with more than twice the mass of all other planets combined
Famous for the Great Red Spot, an enormous anticyclonic storm raging for centuries
Has a faint dust ring system and at least 95 recognized moons

facts_and_myths.claim: Jupiter has a solid rocky surface where astronauts could theoretically land.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Jupiter is composed almost entirely of hydrogen and helium gas transitioning into dense liquid metallic hydrogen at extreme depths.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Jupiter has the shortest day of any solar system planet, completing one rotation in less than 10 hours.

facts_and_myths.claim: Jupiter acts as a giant cosmic vacuum cleaner protecting inner planets from comets.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its immense gravitational field frequently deflects or absorbs rogue comets and asteroids, such as Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In July 1994, fragments of Shoemaker-Levy 9 slammed into Jupiter, leaving Earth-sized black scars in its atmosphere.

name: Uranus
visual_anchor: A pale cyan ice giant planet tilted dramatically on its side, encircled by faint vertical rings against starry darkness.
core_traits: Seventh planet from the Sun and first discovered with a telescope by William Herschel in 1781
Ice giant with an atmosphere rich in hydrogen, helium, and methane giving it an aquamarine blue hue
Rotates on an extreme axial tilt of 98 degrees, essentially rolling on its side around the Sun
Has the coldest planetary atmosphere in the solar system, dropping to -224 degrees Celsius

facts_and_myths.claim: Uranus rotates on its side likely due to a massive cataclysmic ancient collision.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Astronomers hypothesize an Earth-sized protoplanet struck Uranus billions of years ago, tipping its rotational axis over.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its extreme tilt means each pole experiences 42 years of continuous sunlight followed by 42 years of darkness.

facts_and_myths.claim: Uranus has no rings like Saturn.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Uranus possesses 13 distinct narrow dark rings composed of dark boulders and dust particles.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: All 27 moons of Uranus are named after literary characters created by William Shakespeare and Alexander Pope.

name: Neptune
visual_anchor: A deep cobalt-blue ice giant encircled by delicate faint rings and white cirrus clouds whipped by supersonic storms.
core_traits: Eighth and most distant recognized planet from the Sun in the solar system
Ice giant planet colored vivid deep azure due to atmospheric methane gas
Hosts the fastest wind speeds measured anywhere in the solar system, exceeding 2,100 km/h
Discovered in 1846 through mathematical predictions based on gravitational perturbations of Uranus

facts_and_myths.claim: Neptune was discovered through mathematical calculation before being seen through a telescope.
facts_and_myths.explanation: French mathematician Urbain Le Verrier calculated its exact position by analyzing wobbles in Uranus's orbit.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Johann Galle discovered Neptune through a telescope at the Berlin Observatory within one degree of Le Verrier's predicted spot.

facts_and_myths.claim: Neptune is always the most distant major or dwarf planet in the solar system.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Due to Pluto's eccentric elliptical orbit, Pluto occasionally moves closer to the Sun than Neptune for 20-year intervals.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Between 1979 and 1999, Neptune was actually further from the Sun than Pluto.

name: Pluto
visual_anchor: A russet and cream-colored dwarf planet showcasing a vast bright heart-shaped nitrogen ice plain called Tombaugh Regio.
core_traits: Famous icy dwarf planet located in the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune
Classified as the ninth major planet from 1930 until reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006
Features a prominent bright heart-shaped nitrogen glacier known as Sputnik Planitia
Has five known moons, the largest of which is Charon

facts_and_myths.claim: Pluto is physically larger than Earth's Moon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Pluto is significantly smaller than the Moon; its diameter is 2,377 km compared to the Moon's 3,474 km.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pluto is smaller in surface area than the continent of South America.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pluto and its moon Charon form a binary dwarf planet system.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their center of gravity (barycenter) lies in open space outside Pluto's surface, making them orbit each other.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: NASA's New Horizons probe performed the historic first flyby of Pluto in July 2015.

name: Ceres
visual_anchor: A round cratered grey dwarf planet displaying bright glowing salt deposits inside Occator Crater in the asteroid belt.
core_traits: Largest object in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter
Only dwarf planet located within the inner solar system
Contains approximately one-third of the total mass of the entire asteroid belt
Famous for mysterious reflective bright spots of sodium carbonate inside Occator Crater

facts_and_myths.claim: Ceres was historically considered a full planet for half a century after its discovery.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Discovered by Giuseppe Piazzi in 1801, Ceres was listed as a planet alongside Mars and Jupiter until demoted to asteroid.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: NASA's Dawn spacecraft orbited Ceres from 2015 to 2018, revealing signs of cryovolcanism (ice volcanoes).

facts_and_myths.claim: The bright white spots on Ceres are fields of radioactive diamonds.
facts_and_myths.explanation: High-resolution data from the Dawn mission confirmed the bright spots are sodium carbonate salt minerals left by evaporating briny water.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ceres may harbor a subsurface ocean of salty liquid water beneath its crust.

name: Eris
visual_anchor: A shimmering frosty trans-Neptunian dwarf planet gleaming white in deep distant space accompanied by tiny moon Dysnomia.
core_traits: Massive icy dwarf planet located in the scattered disc beyond the Kuiper Belt
Its discovery in 2005 directly triggered the IAU decision to redefine planet criteria and reclassify Pluto
Second-largest known dwarf planet in the solar system, slightly smaller in diameter than Pluto but 27% more massive
Has one known natural moon named Dysnomia

facts_and_myths.claim: The discovery of Eris was the direct reason Pluto lost its official major planet status.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because Eris was more massive than Pluto, astronomers had to either designate Eris as the tenth planet or create the dwarf planet category.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Eris was named after the Greek goddess of discord and strife because of the fierce debate its discovery ignited.

facts_and_myths.claim: Eris orbits the Sun faster than Pluto.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Eris is three times farther from the Sun than Pluto and takes roughly 558 Earth years to complete one single orbit.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: At its surface, the Sun appears as nothing more than an intensely bright pinpoint of starlight.

name: Haumea
visual_anchor: An elongated oval dwarf planet shaped like an American football spinning rapidly with a crystalline ice ring.
core_traits: Dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt notable for its distinctly elongated, rugby-football shape
Rotates at blistering speed once every 3.9 hours, stretching it into an ellipsoid
Possesses a ring system and two small moons named Hi'iaka and Namaka
Surface is covered in brilliant crystalline water ice

facts_and_myths.claim: Haumea has the fastest rotation of any known equilibrium body in the solar system.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its 3.9-hour spin is so rapid that centrifugal force distorts what would be a spherical body into a three-axis triaxial ellipsoid.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Haumea was named after the Hawaiian goddess of fertility and childbirth.

facts_and_myths.claim: Haumea is completely spherical just like Earth and Pluto.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Haumea's long axis is roughly twice the length of its shortest axis, making it resemble an American football.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In 2017, astronomers observed Haumea occult a star and discovered it possesses a narrow ring system.

name: Makemake
visual_anchor: A reddish frozen dwarf planet covered in frozen methane sheets drifting silently through the Kuiper Belt.
core_traits: Dwarf planet and classical Kuiper Belt object discovered shortly after Easter in 2005
Has a reddish tint caused by tholins formed from frozen methane and ethane
Lacks a significant atmosphere due to freezing cold temperatures hovering around 30 Kelvin
Orbits the Sun every 306 Earth years

facts_and_myths.claim: Makemake was named after the creator god of the Rapa Nui people of Easter Island.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because it was discovered shortly after Easter, the team chose Makemake, chief creator deity of Rapa Nui mythology.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its provisional nickname among its discovery team was 'Easterbunny'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Makemake is encircled by an immense ring system larger than Saturn's.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Makemake has no detected ring system, although the Hubble Space Telescope discovered a tiny dark moon nicknamed MK2 in 2016.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Makemake is the second brightest Kuiper Belt object in the night sky after Pluto.

name: Ganymede
visual_anchor: A massive grooved icy moon orbiting Jupiter, larger than planet Mercury and boasting dark cratered terrain.
core_traits: Largest moon in the solar system, orbiting the gas giant Jupiter
Only moon in the solar system known to possess its own internally generated magnetic field
Larger in diameter than the planet Mercury and dwarf planet Pluto
Harbors a subsurface saltwater ocean containing more water than all of Earth's oceans combined

facts_and_myths.claim: Ganymede is physically larger in diameter than the planet Mercury.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ganymede has a diameter of 5,268 km, whereas Mercury measures 4,879 km across.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: If Ganymede orbited the Sun rather than Jupiter, it would be officially classified as a major planet.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ganymede's magnetic field is caused by human spacecraft radio emissions.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its magnetic field is naturally generated by convection within its molten iron-rich core, exactly like Earth's dynamo.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ganymede's ocean is sandwiched between thick layers of high-pressure ice.

name: Titan
visual_anchor: An amber-shrouded moon enveloped in thick nitrogen smog, hosting gleaming liquid methane lakes under hazy orange skies.
core_traits: Largest moon of Saturn and the second-largest moon in the solar system
Only natural satellite with a dense atmosphere and the only extraterrestrial body with liquid surface lakes and seas
Weather cycle features clouds, rain, and rivers of liquid hydrocarbons such as methane and ethane
Successfully visited by ESA's Huygens probe, which landed on its surface in 2005

facts_and_myths.claim: A human could strap on artificial wings and fly through Titan's atmosphere under muscle power.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because Titan has low gravity (0.14g) and a dense atmosphere (1.5x Earth's surface pressure), human-powered flight is theoretically possible.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Titan's largest lake, Kraken Mare, is larger than the Caspian Sea on Earth.

facts_and_myths.claim: The lakes on Titan are filled with liquid freshwater like lakes on Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Temperatures on Titan are -179 degrees Celsius, meaning water ice behaves like rock; its liquid lakes consist of liquid methane and ethane.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: NASA is designing the Dragonfly quadcopter drone to fly across the dunes of Titan in the 2030s.

name: Callisto
visual_anchor: An ancient, dark, heavily cratered moon of Jupiter sparkling with billions of ice-rimmed impact craters.
core_traits: Second-largest moon of Jupiter and third-largest moon in the solar system
Most heavily cratered object known in the solar system, with a surface billions of years old
Lacks volcanic or tectonic activity, leaving an ancient unrenewed geologic record
Features the massive multi-ring impact basin known as Valhalla

facts_and_myths.claim: Callisto has the oldest, most heavily cratered surface in the entire solar system.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Almost completely undisturbed by tectonic forces or volcanism, its craters have accumulated continuously for 4 billion years.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Callisto's surface is essentially saturated with craters - new impacts merely obliterate older ones.

facts_and_myths.claim: Callisto is intensely radioactive compared to Jupiter's other Galilean moons.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because it orbits outside Jupiter's main radiation belt, Callisto has the lowest radiation levels of any Galilean moon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its low radiation environment makes Callisto a leading candidate for a future crewed base camp in the Jovian system.

name: Io
visual_anchor: A mottled sulfurous yellow and orange moon spewing towering plumes of sulfur volcanic gas against Jupiter's swirling storms.
core_traits: Innermost of the four Galilean moons orbiting Jupiter
Most geologically active body in the entire solar system, boasting over 400 active volcanoes
Mottled yellow, orange, and black surface earned it the popular nickname 'Pizza Moon'
Volcanic activity is driven by intense gravitational tidal heating from Jupiter and neighboring moons

facts_and_myths.claim: Io's volcanic eruptions can blast sulfur plumes hundreds of kilometers into space.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Volcanoes like Pele shoot plumes of sulfur gas and silicate magma over 500 kilometers above the surface.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Lava flows on Io can reach temperatures exceeding 1,300 degrees Celsius, hotter than typical basaltic lava on Earth.

facts_and_myths.claim: Io's intense heat is generated by radioactive uranium fuel in its core.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Io's heat comes from tidal flexing: Jupiter's intense gravity combined with resonances from Europa and Ganymede kneads Io like dough.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Io cuts through Jupiter's magnetic field, acting as an electrical generator producing 3 million amperes of current.

name: Europa
visual_anchor: A pristine cracked alabaster moon crisscrossed by intricate reddish fractures hiding a global subsurface liquid ocean.
core_traits: Smallest of Jupiter's four Galilean moons, slightly smaller than Earth's Moon
Possesses the smoothest known surface of any solid body in the solar system
Crisscrossed by reddish-brown linear cracks called lineae caused by tidal stresses
Harbors a global liquid saltwater ocean beneath an icy crust 15 to 25 kilometers thick

facts_and_myths.claim: Europa's subsurface ocean may contain more than twice the liquid water of all Earth's oceans combined.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Although Europa is smaller than the Moon, its global ocean is estimated to be 60 to 150 kilometers deep.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hydrothermal vents on Europa's seafloor are considered among the most promising sites to search for extraterrestrial life.

facts_and_myths.claim: The reddish lines on Europa are massive superhighways built by alien civilizations.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They are tectonic fracture ridges filled with mineral-rich brines and sulfur salts welling up from beneath the ice crust.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: NASA launched the Europa Clipper spacecraft in 2024 to conduct dozens of low-altitude flybys.

name: Enceladus
visual_anchor: A dazzling snow-white icy moon erupting massive plumes of watery cryovolcanic geysers from tiger-stripe fissures into space.
core_traits: Sixth-largest moon of Saturn, known for its brilliant reflective surface of fresh clean ice
Discovered to shoot spectacular cryovolcanic plumes of water vapor and organic molecules from south polar geysers
Material erupted from its geysers creates and feeds Saturn's sprawling E-ring
Harbors a regional or global subsurface liquid water ocean in direct contact with a rocky seafloor

facts_and_myths.claim: Enceladus has the most reflective surface of any body in the solar system.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because it is continually recoated in fresh fine ice particles from its geysers, it reflects nearly 100% of the sunlight hitting it.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Cassini spacecraft flew directly through Enceladus's geyser plumes, detecting water vapor, molecular hydrogen, and complex organics.

facts_and_myths.claim: The geysers of Enceladus spew boiling molten rock lava.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Enceladus exhibits cryovolcanism - its geysers vent superheated water vapor, simple organic chemicals, and ice crystals.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The four parallel fracture grooves at its south pole are famously named 'Tiger Stripes'.

name: Triton
visual_anchor: A frost-encrusted moon exhibiting cantaloupe-patterned plains and dark nitrogen geysers rising beneath the blue disk of Neptune.
core_traits: Largest moon of Neptune and the only large moon in the solar system with a retrograde orbit
Likely a captured Kuiper Belt dwarf planet closely related to Pluto
Surface features unique dimpled terrain known as 'cantaloupe terrain'
Active nitrogen ice geysers erupt plumes up to 8 kilometers high into its tenuous atmosphere

facts_and_myths.claim: Triton is slowly spiraling toward Neptune and will eventually be shredded into a magnificent ring.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tidal deceleration in its retrograde orbit pulls Triton inward; within 3.6 billion years it will cross the Roche limit and break apart.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Triton is one of the coldest objects ever measured in our solar system, with a surface temperature of -235 degrees Celsius.

facts_and_myths.claim: Triton formed in the same orbit alongside Neptune during the initial birth of the solar system.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its retrograde orbit and dwarf planet composition prove it was a Kuiper Belt object captured by Neptune's immense gravity.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Voyager 2 is the only human spacecraft to have visited Triton, flying past in August 1989.

name: Phobos
visual_anchor: A heavily grooved, potato-shaped dark asteroid-like moon skimming perilously close above the rust-red plains of Mars.
core_traits: Larger and innermost of the two natural moons of Mars
Orbits closer to its primary planet than any other moon in the solar system, just 6,000 km above Mars
Dominated by Stickney Crater, a giant impact basin nearly half the moon's diameter
Orbits Mars three times in a single Martian day

facts_and_myths.claim: Phobos is doomed to crash into Mars or shatter into a ring of rubble.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because it orbits inside the synchronous orbit radius, tidal drag draws it closer by 2 meters every century until it breaks apart in 30-50 million years.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: From the surface of Mars, Phobos rises in the west and sets in the east twice every Martian day.

facts_and_myths.claim: Stickney Crater was created by an ancient artificial laser cannon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Stickney Crater was gouged by a natural meteorite impact so powerful it nearly shattered Phobos into pieces.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Phobos is named after the Greek god of fear and panic, brother of Deimos.

name: Deimos
visual_anchor: A smooth, lumpy miniature moon covered in a thick blanket of dust drifting peacefully high above Mars.
core_traits: Smaller and outermost of the two natural moons of planet Mars
Tiny irregular non-spherical body measuring only about 12 kilometers across
Appears smooth because many craters are buried beneath a thick layer of loose regolith
Takes 30.3 hours to complete an orbit around Mars

facts_and_myths.claim: Escape velocity on Deimos is so low that a person could jump off into outer space on a bicycle.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With an escape velocity of just 20 km/h (5.6 m/s), an athletic human sprinting on a ramp could achieve orbital escape.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Seen from Mars, Deimos looks barely brighter than Venus appears from Earth.

facts_and_myths.claim: Deimos has active geysers venting steam into the Martian sky.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Deimos is a cold, dead, airless rock with zero geological activity or internal heat.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The United Arab Emirates Hope spacecraft captured the closest, most detailed images of Deimos in 2023.

name: Charon
visual_anchor: A rugged grey moon crowned with a distinctive reddish-brown north polar cap known as Mordor Macula, facing Pluto.
core_traits: Largest moon of dwarf planet Pluto, discovered in 1978 by James Christy
So massive relative to Pluto (roughly half its diameter) that they share a mutual barycenter in open space
Tidally locked to Pluto so both bodies permanently show the exact same face to each other
Features a distinct dark reddish polar cap nicknamed Mordor Macula

facts_and_myths.claim: Charon never rises or sets in the sky from any given spot on Pluto.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because Pluto and Charon are mutually tidally locked, Charon hangs motionless in the sky or remains forever below the horizon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The red color at Charon's north pole is caused by methane escaping Pluto's atmosphere and getting trapped and baked by ultraviolet light.

facts_and_myths.claim: Charon was named after an astronaut who walked on Mars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Discoverer James Christy named it Charon after the mythological ferryman of Hades who carried souls across the River Styx, blending it with his wife Charlene's nickname 'Char'.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Charon has a canyon system deeper and longer than Earth's Grand Canyon.

name: Comet Halley
visual_anchor: A blazing icy comet trailing a radiant turquoise ion tail and sweeping white dust plume across the night sky.
core_traits: Most famous periodic comet in human history, visible to the naked eye from Earth every 75 to 76 years
First comet recognized as periodic by English astronomer Edmond Halley in 1705
Only known short-period comet that is regularly visible to the naked eye twice in a single human lifetime
Parent body responsible for the Orionid and Eta Aquariid meteor showers

facts_and_myths.claim: Mark Twain was born in a year Halley's Comet appeared and died the day after it returned.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Twain was born on November 30, 1835 (two weeks after perihelion) and died on April 21, 1910 (the day after perihelion).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Halley's Comet will make its next dramatic approach to Earth in mid-2061.

facts_and_myths.claim: Comet Halley's nucleus is a blindingly bright white snowball.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Giotto spacecraft revealed Halley's nucleus is pitch-black, reflecting only about 4% of light - darker than charcoal.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its presence was famously embroidered into the 11th-century Bayeux Tapestry depicting the Norman Conquest.

name: Comet Hale-Bopp
visual_anchor: A magnificent celestial comet displaying twin sweeping tails - one brilliant golden dust and one glowing electric-blue gas.
core_traits: One of the most widely observed and brightest comets of the 20th century
Remained visible to the naked eye for a record-shattering 18 continuous months in 1996 and 1997
Possessed an unusually huge nucleus measuring approximately 60 kilometers in diameter
Has an orbital period estimated between 2,500 and 4,000 years

facts_and_myths.claim: Comet Hale-Bopp was visible to the naked eye longer than any other comet recorded in history.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It was visible without binoculars or telescopes for 18 months, twice as long as the previous record holder, the Great Comet of 1811.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Co-discovered independently by amateur astronomer Alan Hale and Thomas Bopp on July 23, 1995.

facts_and_myths.claim: An alien mothership was trailing directly behind Hale-Bopp's nucleus.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The claim was an internet hoax propagated by amateur radio enthusiasts, which tragically inspired the Heaven's Gate cult tragedy in 1997.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hale-Bopp produced an extremely rare third tail made entirely of neutral sodium atoms.

name: Comet NEOWISE
visual_anchor: A glowing white and yellow comet with a dramatic split tail soaring above twilight horizons during the summer of 2020.
core_traits: Spectacular long-period comet discovered in March 2020 by the NEOWISE space telescope
Became the brightest comet visible from the Northern Hemisphere since Hale-Bopp in 1997
Survived perihelion passage inside Mercury's orbit without disintegrating
Its orbital period was altered by planetary gravity to roughly 6,800 years

facts_and_myths.claim: Comet NEOWISE will not return to the inner solar system for nearly 7,000 years.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Gravitational interactions with planets expanded its orbital period from 4,500 years to approximately 6,800 years.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Astronauts aboard the International Space Station captured stunning time-lapse videos of NEOWISE rising above Earth's aurora.

facts_and_myths.claim: NEOWISE collided with the Sun and was completely vaporized.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It successfully rounded the Sun on July 3, 2020, passing within 43 million kilometers before flying back toward deep space.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The comet nucleus is about 5 kilometers across and coated in dark soot.

name: Asteroid Belt
visual_anchor: Vast ring of rocky, metallic, and carbonaceous asteroids orbiting the Sun in the quiet expanse between Mars and Jupiter.
core_traits: Circumstellar disc located between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter
Contains millions of irregular rocky bodies, including dwarf planet Ceres and asteroids Vesta and Pallas
Total mass is estimated at only about 4% of the mass of Earth's Moon
Formed from primordial solar nebula material that never coalesced into a planet due to Jupiter's gravitational disruption

facts_and_myths.claim: Navigating through the asteroid belt requires frantic swerving like in science fiction movies.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Space is vast; the average distance between asteroids is roughly 1 million kilometers, making accidental collisions virtually impossible.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dozens of robotic spacecraft have traversed the asteroid belt without a single accidental collision.

facts_and_myths.claim: Over half the entire mass of the asteroid belt is concentrated in just four large bodies.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ceres, Vesta, Pallas, and Hygiea together make up more than 50% of the entire belt's collective mass.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ceres alone accounts for approximately 39% of the total mass.

name: Kuiper Belt
visual_anchor: A colossal donut-shaped ring of icy planetesimals, comets, and frozen dwarf planets spanning beyond the orbit of Neptune.
core_traits: Circumstellar disc in the outer solar system extending from the orbit of Neptune (30 AU) to approximately 50 AU
Composed mostly of small frozen volatile bodies made of water, ammonia, and methane ice
Home to recognized dwarf planets Pluto, Haumea, and Makemake
Source region for most short-period comets that orbit the Sun in under 200 years

facts_and_myths.claim: The Kuiper Belt is vastly larger and more massive than the main asteroid belt.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is roughly 20 times as wide and 20 to 200 times as massive as the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Gerard Kuiper proposed the belt in 1951, but the first true Kuiper Belt object after Pluto was discovered in 1992.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Kuiper Belt marks the absolute boundary where the Sun's gravity completely ends.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Sun's gravitational influence extends thousands of times farther out to the Oort Cloud, nearly halfway to the nearest star.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: NASA's New Horizons spacecraft explored the Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth in 2019, revealing a pristine contact binary shaped like a snowman.

name: Oort Cloud
visual_anchor: An immense, ethereal spherical shell of billions of icy comets enveloping the outermost perimeter of the entire solar system.
core_traits: Theoretical immense spherical shell of icy planetesimals surrounding the solar system
Extends from roughly 2,000 AU out to as far as 100,000 to 200,000 AU (nearly 3 light-years) from the Sun
Defines the true cosmological boundary of the Sun's gravitational dominance
Origin and reservoir for long-period comets with orbital periods of thousands to millions of years

facts_and_myths.claim: The outer edge of the Oort Cloud extends almost halfway to Proxima Centauri, the nearest star.
facts_and_myths.explanation: At nearly 100,000 astronomical units, its outer reaches brush the gravitational boundaries of neighboring star systems.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It would take Voyager 1 roughly 300 years to reach the inner Oort Cloud and about 30,000 years to exit its outer edge.

facts_and_myths.claim: Astronomers have captured direct close-up high-resolution photographs of Oort Cloud comets.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because objects in the Oort Cloud are tiny, dark, and light-years away, no human telescope has directly resolved them in place.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dutch astronomer Jan Oort proposed the cloud in 1950 to explain why new long-period comets keep arriving without running out.

name: Olympus Mons
visual_anchor: A gargantuan shield volcano towering into the thin Martian stratosphere, spanning an area as large as France.
core_traits: Colossal shield volcano on Mars and the tallest mountain and volcano in the entire solar system
Stands approximately 21.9 kilometers high, about two and a half times the height of Mount Everest
Base diameter spans over 600 kilometers, approximately equivalent to the state of Arizona or country of France
Grew to enormous proportions because Mars lacks mobile tectonic plates, allowing stationary magma plumes to erupt in one spot for billions of years

facts_and_myths.claim: A person standing at the base of Olympus Mons would not realize they are on a mountain.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because the volcano's slope is so gentle (only 2 to 5 degrees) and Mars has high curvature, the summit lies beyond the horizon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The summit caldera is a complex volcanic sink 80 kilometers wide and 3 kilometers deep.

facts_and_myths.claim: Olympus Mons is currently erupting massive rivers of glowing molten lava.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Olympus Mons is dormant or extinct, with the most recent volcanic activity estimated to have occurred tens of millions of years ago.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its summit peeks out above most of the Martian atmosphere, bathed in near-vacuum.

name: Great Red Spot
visual_anchor: A swirling crimson anticyclonic vortex churning furiously across the clouds of Jupiter, larger than planet Earth.
core_traits: Persistent anticyclonic storm located 22 degrees south of Jupiter's equator
Has been observed continuously for at least 190 years, and possibly as early as 1665 by Giovanni Cassini
Spans a diameter greater than Earth's, with internal counterclockwise wind speeds exceeding 430 km/h
Red coloration is thought to arise from cosmic ray interactions with ammonium hydrosulfide and phosphorus

facts_and_myths.claim: The Great Red Spot is large enough to swallow the entire planet Earth whole.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Even after shrinking in recent decades to 16,350 km across, it remains wider than Earth's 12,742 km diameter.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the late 19th century, the storm was large enough to fit three Earths side-by-side.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Great Red Spot is a permanent solid island floating on Jupiter's surface.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Jupiter has no solid surface; the Great Red Spot is a purely atmospheric weather storm trapped between opposing jet streams.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: NASA's Juno spacecraft found the storm extends at least 300 to 500 kilometers deep into Jupiter's atmosphere.

name: Valles Marineris
visual_anchor: A titanic canyon system tearing across the red equator of Mars, plunging into shadowed chasms four times deeper than the Grand Canyon.
core_traits: Vast system of canyons running along the Martian equator just east of the Tharsis volcanic region
Spans over 4,000 kilometers in length, nearly one-fifth of the circumference of Mars
Reaches depths of up to 7 kilometers and widths of up to 200 kilometers
Formed as a colossal tectonic crack opened by the uplift and swelling of the neighboring Tharsis volcanic plateau

facts_and_myths.claim: Valles Marineris is long enough to span the entire continental United States from New York to San Francisco.
facts_and_myths.explanation: At 4,000 km long, it easily exceeds the width of the contiguous United States, making Earth's Grand Canyon look tiny in comparison.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It was named in honor of NASA's Mariner 9 orbiter, which discovered it during the first planetary orbital mapping mission in 1971-1972.

facts_and_myths.claim: Valles Marineris was carved entirely by a giant rushing river of liquid water.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Unlike Earth's Grand Canyon which was carved by water erosion, Valles Marineris is primarily a massive tectonic rift valley widened by landslides.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Morning fogs of water ice frequently form in the lowest depths of its canyon floors.

name: Solar Wind
visual_anchor: A shimmering stream of glowing ionized plasma hurtling outward from the Sun's corona, buffeting planetary magnetospheres.
core_traits: Continuous stream of charged particles (mostly protons and electrons) released from the Sun's upper atmosphere
Speeds range from 250 to over 750 kilometers per second as it sweeps across the solar system
Shapes planetary magnetospheres and blows comet tails away from the Sun
Interacts with Earth's magnetic field to generate the spectacular Aurora Borealis and Aurora Australis

facts_and_myths.claim: A comet's tail points away from the Sun because of solar wind pressure, not the direction of comet travel.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Radiation pressure and the solar wind continually push ionized gas and dust outward from the Sun, regardless of the comet's motion.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Solar sails use radiation pressure from sunlight and solar wind to propel deep-space spacecraft without chemical fuel.

facts_and_myths.claim: The solar wind blows away Earth's atmosphere completely on a daily basis.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Earth's strong magnetic field deflects the solar wind around the planet like water around the bow of a ship.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mars lost most of its primordial atmosphere over billions of years because it lacked a global magnetic field to fend off the solar wind.

name: Solar Flare
visual_anchor: A blinding flash of electromagnetic radiation exploding violently from a twisted magnetic sunspot loop on the Sun's surface.
core_traits: Intense localized burst of electromagnetic radiation in the Sun's atmosphere caused by magnetic reconnection
Releases energy equivalent to millions of 100-megaton hydrogen bombs exploding simultaneously
Travels at the speed of light, reaching Earth in just over 8 minutes
Can cause immediate high-frequency radio blackouts on the sunlit side of Earth

facts_and_myths.claim: Solar flares travel at the speed of light and can disrupt Earth's radio communications within 8 minutes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because solar flares are bursts of electromagnetic radiation (X-rays and ultraviolet light), they travel at the speed of light across space.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Solar flares are classified into letter categories: A, B, C, M, and X, with X-class being the most powerful.

facts_and_myths.claim: A solar flare can vaporize humanity off the face of the Earth in an instant.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Earth's atmosphere absorbs harmful X-rays and ultraviolet radiation, preventing deadly radiation from reaching the surface.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The largest solar flare recorded by modern satellites in 2003 saturated X-ray sensors, estimated at X28 to X45.

name: Coronal Mass Ejection
visual_anchor: A colossal bubble of billions of tons of magnetized solar plasma erupting into interplanetary space from the Sun's corona.
core_traits: Significant release of plasma and accompanying magnetic field from the solar corona into space
Hurls billions of tons of coronal material at speeds up to 3,000 km/s
Takes 1 to 3 days to travel the 150 million kilometers to Earth
Can trigger severe geomagnetic storms, induce power grid failures, and disable orbiting satellites

facts_and_myths.claim: A massive CME struck Earth in 1859, causing telegraph wires to catch fire and shock operators.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Carrington Event of 1859 was a massive CME collision that induced powerful currents in telegraph lines worldwide.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: During the Carrington Event, auroras were so intensely bright that gold miners in the Rocky Mountains woke up and cooked breakfast at 2 a.m.

facts_and_myths.claim: A Coronal Mass Ejection and a Solar Flare are the exact same physical phenomenon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A flare is a burst of electromagnetic light arriving in 8 minutes, whereas a CME is a physical cloud of billions of tons of plasma taking days to arrive.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In July 2012, an ultra-powerful Carrington-class CME narrowly missed Earth by just 9 days.

name: Sunspot
visual_anchor: Dark magnetic blemishes with dark centers and lighter radial penumbras freckling the brilliant yellow face of the Sun.
core_traits: Temporary dark spots on the Sun's photosphere caused by concentrated magnetic field flux
Appear dark only by contrast because they are roughly 1,500 degrees Celsius cooler than the surrounding 5,500 degrees Celsius surface
Serve as the birthplace and launch points for major solar flares and coronal mass ejections
Follow a roughly 11-year solar activity cycle of maximums and minimums

facts_and_myths.claim: Sunspots are cold, pitch-black voids on the Sun.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sunspots are extremely hot (around 4,000 degrees Celsius); if a sunspot were placed isolated in the night sky, it would glow brighter than the full Moon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some sunspots are large enough to comfortably fit several Earths across their dark core (umbra).

facts_and_myths.claim: The number of sunspots follows an 11-year cycle from solar minimum to solar maximum.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Heinrich Schwabe discovered the 11-year solar cycle in 1843 after meticulously recording sunspot numbers for 17 years.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: During the Maunder Minimum (1645-1715), sunspots almost completely disappeared, coinciding with Europe's 'Little Ice Age'.

name: Solar Eclipse
visual_anchor: A pitch-black lunar silhouette perfectly covering the Sun, revealing the ethereal glowing silver wisps of the solar corona in daytime.
core_traits: Celestial event where the Moon passes directly between the Sun and Earth, fully or partially blocking sunlight
Total eclipses cast a narrow shadow called the umbra across Earth's surface where daytime briefly turns to twilight
Reveals the Sun's ethereal outer atmosphere (corona), normally invisible against daytime glare
Possible only because the Sun is 400 times wider than the Moon and also 400 times farther away

facts_and_myths.claim: A total solar eclipse is only possible because the Sun is roughly 400 times larger than the Moon and 400 times farther away.
facts_and_myths.explanation: This incredible cosmic coincidence makes the apparent angular size of the Moon and Sun nearly identical (about 0.5 degrees) from Earth.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Because the Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at 3.8 cm per year, total solar eclipses will cease to exist in about 600 million years.

facts_and_myths.claim: It is safe to stare directly at the Sun with naked eyes during a partial solar eclipse.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Looking directly at the Sun during any partial phase causes permanent retinal solar burns; specialized ISO-certified eclipse glasses are required.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: During totality, strange dancing bands of dark and light shadows called 'shadow bands' ripple across the ground.

name: Lunar Eclipse
visual_anchor: A full moon bathed in an eerie deep copper-red glow as it passes through the dark central shadow of Earth.
core_traits: Astronomical event occurring when Earth comes directly between the Sun and Moon, casting its shadow across the lunar surface
Can only take place during a full moon when the Sun, Earth, and Moon align in syzygy
The Moon turns a dramatic reddish-copper color known as a 'Blood Moon'
Safe to view with the naked eye from anywhere on Earth's night hemisphere

facts_and_myths.claim: The Moon turns blood-red during a lunar eclipse because of all the sunrises and sunsets happening around Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Earth's atmosphere bends (refracts) sunlight, scattering blue light and projecting the combined red glow of all Earth's sunsets onto the Moon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: If you stood on the Moon during a total lunar eclipse, you would see Earth surrounded by a glowing fiery red ring.

facts_and_myths.claim: Lunar eclipses happen every single month whenever there is a full moon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Moon's orbit is tilted about 5 degrees relative to Earth's orbital plane, so its shadow usually passes above or below Earth.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Unlike solar eclipses which last minutes, total lunar eclipses can last for over an hour.

name: Transit of Venus
visual_anchor: A crisp black circular silhouette of Venus creeping slowly across the brilliant golden face of the Sun.
core_traits: Rare astronomical transit where the planet Venus passes directly between the Sun and Earth
Appears as a distinct tiny black dot crawling across the solar disk over several hours
Occurs in an unusual pattern repeating every 243 years: pairs separated by 8 years, then gaps of over a century
Historically used by 18th-century astronomers to calculate the absolute distance from Earth to the Sun (the Astronomical Unit)

facts_and_myths.claim: No human alive today will witness another Transit of Venus unless they live past the year 2117.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Following the historic transits of 2004 and 2012, the next transit of Venus will not occur until December 11, 2117.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Captain James Cook's famous first voyage to Tahiti in 1769 was commissioned by the Royal Society to observe the Transit of Venus.

facts_and_myths.claim: Venus completely blocks out sunlight and plunges Earth into darkness during a transit.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Venus is so distant that it covers only about 0.1% of the solar disk, appearing merely as a small black bead.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mikhail Lomonosov discovered that Venus has an atmosphere in 1761 after observing a halo of light refract around its edge during a transit.

name: Asteroid Bennu
visual_anchor: A dark diamond-shaped spinning rubble-pile asteroid strewn with jagged boulders floating in near-Earth space.
core_traits: Carbonaceous near-Earth asteroid classified as a potentially hazardous asteroid
Shaped like a spinning top, composed of a loose gravity-bound collection of rock rubble
Target of NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission, which successfully collected surface samples in 2020 and returned them to Earth in 2023
Contains primordial organic molecules and water-bearing clay minerals dating back to the birth of the solar system

facts_and_myths.claim: NASA's OSIRIS-REx spacecraft sank into Bennu's surface like a ball in a children's plastic ball pit.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Bennu's surface has almost no cohesion; the probe's sampling arm penetrated deeply into the asteroid with virtually zero resistance.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The sample capsule parachuted into the Utah desert on September 24, 2023, delivering 121 grams of pristine asteroid material.

facts_and_myths.claim: Asteroid Bennu is guaranteed to collide with Earth and destroy civilization in the next 10 years.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Calculations indicate a cumulative 1-in-1,750 chance of impact between 2178 and 2290, with September 24, 2182 being the most significant date.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bennu was named after an ancient Egyptian mythological heron associated with the Sun, creation, and rebirth.

name: Asteroid Ryugu
visual_anchor: A spinning dark top-shaped carbonaceous asteroid covered in rugged black boulders visited by Japan's Hayabusa2.
core_traits: Diamond-shaped near-Earth asteroid explored by Japan's Hayabusa2 spacecraft
Rubble-pile asteroid rich in carbon, water-bearing minerals, and amino acids
Hayabusa2 deployed rovers and blasted an artificial impact crater to sample subsurface material in 2019
Successfully returned 5.4 grams of pristine asteroid material to Earth in December 2020

facts_and_myths.claim: Laboratory analysis of Ryugu samples discovered over 20 different amino acids essential for life.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The pristine samples contained glycine, alanine, and other prebiotic organic compounds untouched by Earth's atmosphere.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ryugu was named after the mythical underwater 'Dragon Palace' (Ryugu-jo) from Japanese folklore.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ryugu is a solid block of pure gold and titanium.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ryugu is a loose 'rubble pile' held together by weak gravity, with high porosity and composed mostly of carbonaceous rock.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hayabusa2 fired a 2.5 kg copper projectile into Ryugu to create a crater and retrieve unweathered underground rocks.

name: Asteroid Psyche
visual_anchor: A massive gleaming metallic potato-shaped asteroid composed of exposed iron-nickel metal drifting in the main belt.
core_traits: One of the most massive objects in the main asteroid belt, measuring over 220 km across
Unique M-type asteroid thought to be the exposed metallic iron-nickel core of a shattered early protoplanet
Target of NASA's dedicated Psyche spacecraft mission launched in October 2023
Offers scientists a unique direct window into planetary core formation that is inaccessible inside Earth

facts_and_myths.claim: Psyche contains enough precious metals to make every human on Earth a billionaire if mined.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its iron, nickel, and gold content has a theoretical commodity value estimated at 10 quintillion dollars, though bringing it to Earth would collapse metal markets.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: NASA's Psyche spacecraft uses solar electric Hall-effect thrusters and will arrive at the asteroid in 2029.

facts_and_myths.claim: Psyche was discovered by modern radar satellites in 2020.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Italian astronomer Annibale de Gasparis discovered Psyche with an optical telescope in Naples on March 17, 1852.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Psyche is named after the mythological Greek goddess of the soul who married Cupid.

name: Meteor
visual_anchor: A blazing streak of incandescent white and green light shooting across the starry atmosphere over a silent landscape.
core_traits: Visible streak of light produced when a space rock enters Earth's atmosphere at high speed
Friction and air compression heat the particle until it vaporizes in a flash of incandescence
Typically occurs in the mesosphere between 75 and 100 kilometers above Earth's surface
Particularly bright meteors are called fireballs or bolides

facts_and_myths.claim: Most meteors are caused by particles no larger than a grain of sand or a pea.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because they enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds between 11 and 72 km/s, even a millimeter-sized speck creates a brilliant streak of light.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The intense heat vaporizes the meteoroid within seconds, leaving a glowing trail of ionized air.

facts_and_myths.claim: A meteor streak is an actual star falling out of outer space.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Actual stars are millions of times larger than Earth; meteors are tiny specks of space dust burning up in Earth's upper atmosphere.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The color of a meteor reveals its composition: green from nickel, yellow from sodium, and red from nitrogen and oxygen.

name: Meteorite
visual_anchor: A dense dark magnetic space rock featuring a melted black fusion crust resting in the snow of Antarctica.
core_traits: Solid fragment of an asteroid, comet, Moon, or Mars that survives its fiery atmospheric passage and lands on Earth's surface
Categorized into three main types: stony, iron, and stony-iron (pallasites)
Coated in a thin dark glassy layer called a fusion crust created by atmospheric ablation
Often discovered on the ice sheets of Antarctica and desert sands where dark rocks stand out easily

facts_and_myths.claim: Scientists have discovered authentic meteorites on Earth that originated on the planet Mars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ancient asteroid impacts blasted Martian rocks into space, which wandered for millions of years before crashing into Earth as Martian meteorites.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Over 300 Martian meteorites have been identified by matching trapped gas bubbles to the Martian atmosphere measured by Viking landers.

facts_and_myths.claim: Meteorites are glowing red-hot when they hit the ground and will start forest fires.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Space is freezing cold, and atmospheric entry lasts only seconds; the thin molten crust cools rapidly and meteorites are usually cool or room temperature upon landing.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Hoba meteorite in Namibia is the largest known intact meteorite on Earth, weighing over 60 tons.

name: Meteoroid
visual_anchor: A tiny jagged piece of rock and metal tumbling silently through the pitch-black vacuum of interplanetary space.
core_traits: Small rocky or metallic body drifting in outer space, significantly smaller than an asteroid
Ranges in size from a single grain of dust up to one meter across
Becomes a meteor if it enters an atmosphere, and a meteorite if it impacts the ground
Produced primarily by comet disintegrations and asteroid collisions

facts_and_myths.claim: The terms meteoroid, meteor, and meteorite describe the exact same object at three different stages of its journey.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In space it is a meteoroid; burning in the atmosphere it is a meteor; on the ground it is a meteorite.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Micrometeoroids are so small that millions land on Earth every day, settling as microscopic star dust on house rooftops.

facts_and_myths.claim: A meteoroid is always larger than a city block.
facts_and_myths.explanation: By official definition, objects larger than one meter are asteroids, while meteoroids range from dust grains up to 1 meter.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Spacecraft use Whipple shields (multi-layered bumpers) to protect against hypervelocity micrometeoroid impacts.

name: Shooting Star
visual_anchor: A quick brilliant arc of light darting through the constellation of stars above a silhouette of tall pine trees.
core_traits: Popular common cultural name for the atmospheric optical phenomenon of a meteor
Occurs when cosmic dust burns up high in Earth's mesosphere
Tradition across world cultures encourages making a wish when spotting one in the night sky
Lasts typically for a fraction of a second to a few seconds

facts_and_myths.claim: Shooting stars are actually genuine stars dying and plummeting from the galaxy.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Stars are colossal thermonuclear suns light-years away; a shooting star is merely a tiny speck of dust burning in Earth's upper atmosphere.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: On any clear dark night, an observer can typically see 5 to 10 shooting stars per hour.

facts_and_myths.claim: Many shooting stars observed in modern times are actually decommissioned human satellites deorbiting.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Space debris and old satellite components disintegrating in the upper atmosphere create slow-moving, brightly colored fireball streaks.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: During major meteor outbursts like the 1833 Leonids, over 100,000 shooting stars flashed across the sky in a single hour.

name: Perseid Meteor Shower
visual_anchor: Dozens of brilliant white and green meteors radiating from the Perseus constellation across a starry August midnight sky.
core_traits: Prolific meteor shower peaking annually in mid-August as Earth plows through debris from Comet Swift-Tuttle
Radiant point lies in the constellation Perseus
Produces 60 to 100 bright meteors per hour under dark skies, renowned for frequent fireballs
Observed and recorded by stargazers for over 2,000 years

facts_and_myths.claim: The Perseids are nicknamed the 'Tears of Saint Lawrence' in Catholic tradition.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The peak of the meteor shower coincides with the feast day of Saint Lawrence on August 10, martyred in Rome in 258 AD.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The debris stream particles strike Earth's atmosphere at a blistering speed of 59 kilometers per second.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Perseid meteor shower occurs because the constellation Perseus is exploding.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The stars of Perseus are hundreds of light-years away; the meteors only appear to radiate from that perspective direction due to geometry.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Comet Swift-Tuttle, the parent comet, has an enormous 26-kilometer nucleus and will return near Earth in 2126.

name: Geminid Meteor Shower
visual_anchor: Bright, slow-moving multi-colored meteors streaking across a frosty December night sky from the Gemini constellation.
core_traits: One of the most intense and reliable meteor showers of the year, peaking every December
Uniquely caused by debris from a rocky asteroid (3200 Phaethon) rather than an icy comet
Meteors appear to radiate from near the bright star Castor in the constellation Gemini
Capable of producing up to 120 to 150 bright, multicolored meteors per hour under ideal conditions

facts_and_myths.claim: The Geminids originate from a rocky 'rock comet' asteroid named 3200 Phaethon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Unlike almost all other meteor showers spawned by comets, the Geminids are shed by Phaethon as it gets baked close to the Sun.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Because Phaethon is denser than comet dust, Geminid meteors burn deeper and slower in Earth's atmosphere, often glowing yellow, green, or blue.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Geminid meteor shower has been observed regularly since ancient prehistoric times.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Geminids only began appearing in the mid-19th century; before 1862, no records of the shower exist because Jupiter's gravity gradually shifted the debris stream into Earth's path.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The shower has actually been growing stronger over the last century.

name: Lunar Regolith
visual_anchor: Fine abrasive grey powder covering the lunar surface, marked with deep boot prints of Apollo astronauts.
core_traits: Layer of fine, abrasive dust, broken rock, and impact glass covering the solid bedrock of the Moon
Formed over billions of years by relentless micrometeorite bombardment pulverizing lunar surface rocks
Extremely sharp and jagged because there is no wind or water erosion to round its microscopic edges
Smelled distinctively like spent gunpowder to Apollo astronauts returning into the lunar module

facts_and_myths.claim: Apollo astronauts reported that Moon dust smelled like burnt gunpowder.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When astronauts brought lunar dust into the pressurized lunar module cabin, contact with oxygen triggered an odor resembling burnt gunpowder.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Because of electrostatic levitation, tiny grains of lunar dust can float above the Moon's surface during sunrise and sunset.

facts_and_myths.claim: Lunar dust is soft and smooth like fine beach sand.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Without air or water erosion, lunar dust consists of razor-sharp glass shards that ate through Kevlar spacesuit layers and jammed seals.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Lunar regolith contains trapped helium-3 from the solar wind, considered a potential future nuclear fusion fuel.

name: Rings of Saturn
visual_anchor: A breathtaking expanse of gleaming concentric icy rings casting razor-thin shadows across the golden clouds of Saturn.
core_traits: Most extensive and spectacular planetary ring system in the solar system
Composed 99% of pure water ice particles ranging in size from tiny pebbles to house-sized chunks
Span up to 282,000 kilometers across yet average only about 10 meters in physical thickness
Divided into distinct rings (A, B, C, D, E, F, G) separated by gaps like the Cassini Division

facts_and_myths.claim: If Saturn's rings were scaled down to the size of a sheet of paper, they would be thousands of times thinner than the paper.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Spanning nearly 300,000 km wide but only 10 to 30 meters thick, their aspect ratio is far thinner than a razor blade.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Data from NASA's Cassini mission showed that 'ring rain' is pulling ice into Saturn, meaning the rings could vanish in 100 to 300 million years.

facts_and_myths.claim: Saturn's rings are solid sheets of polished metal or glass.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The rings consist of billions of individual, independently orbiting chunks of pure water ice.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Galileo Galilei first saw them in 1610 through his telescope, mistaking them for 'ears' or triple planets.

name: Heliopause
visual_anchor: An invisible cosmic boundary in deep space where the outward rushing solar wind meets the interstellar cold plasma of the galaxy.
core_traits: Outer boundary of the heliosphere where the solar wind's strength is halted by the interstellar medium
Located roughly 120 astronomical units (18 billion kilometers) from the Sun
Crossed by NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft in August 2012 and Voyager 2 in November 2018
Marks the transition where cosmic ray intensity dramatically spikes and interstellar magnetic fields dominate

facts_and_myths.claim: Voyager 1 officially crossed the heliopause in 2012, becoming the first human-made object to enter interstellar space.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Instruments on Voyager 1 detected a sudden drop in solar wind particles and a dramatic surge in galactic cosmic rays.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The heliopause is not a sphere but a teardrop shape carved by the Sun's motion through the interstellar medium.

facts_and_myths.claim: Crossing the heliopause means a spacecraft has completely exited the Sun's gravitational field.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Sun's gravity dominates out to the Oort Cloud, thousands of times farther than the heliopause.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Outside the heliopause, interstellar gas is significantly denser and colder than the solar wind plasma inside.

name: Solar Prominence
visual_anchor: A gigantic looping arch of glowing red-hot plasma anchored to the Sun's surface, reaching hundreds of thousands of kilometers into space.
core_traits: Large, bright gaseous feature extending outward from the Sun's surface into the corona
Anchored to the photosphere and held in place by strong magnetic field loops
Can persist in a stable state for several months or erupt suddenly into a coronal mass ejection
When viewed against the bright solar disk, it appears as a dark streak known as a solar filament

facts_and_myths.claim: A single solar prominence loop can be large enough to comfortably bridge dozens of Earths.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Prominences can stretch over 500,000 kilometers into space, easily spanning dozens of Earth diameters along their arch.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The plasma in a prominence is about 100 times cooler and denser than the surrounding superheated coronal gas.

facts_and_myths.claim: A solar prominence and a solar filament are two completely unrelated phenomena.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They are the exact same physical feature: called a prominence when viewed extending off the edge against dark space, and a filament when seen against the Sun's disk.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Grand Daddy prominence observed in 1946 expanded to over 1.7 million kilometers before dispersing.

name: Black Hole
visual_anchor: An ominous pitch-black sphere bending background starlight into a warped Einstein ring encircled by a white-hot glowing accretion disk.
core_traits: Region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape
Forms when a massive dying star undergoes gravitational collapse at the end of its life
Surrounded by a boundary called the event horizon marking the point of no return
First directly imaged in 2019 by the Event Horizon Telescope at the heart of galaxy M87

facts_and_myths.claim: Black holes act like giant cosmic vacuum cleaners that roam the universe sucking in everything.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Black holes only pull in matter that crosses their event horizon; if our Sun were replaced by an equal-mass black hole, Earth's orbit would not change.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Time slows down drastically near a black hole due to gravitational time dilation.

facts_and_myths.claim: Approaching a black hole causes matter to stretch into long thin strands in a process called spaghettification.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Extreme tidal forces exert drastically stronger gravity on your feet than on your head, stretching objects vertically into noodle shapes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The first black hole candidate ever discovered was Cygnus X-1 in 1964.

name: Supermassive Black Hole
visual_anchor: A titanic black hole containing billions of solar masses, warping space at the glowing core of an active spiral galaxy.
core_traits: Largest type of black hole, containing millions to billions of times the mass of the Sun
Resides at the center of almost all known large galaxies, including our own Milky Way
Drives violent galactic nuclei phenomena such as quasars and relativistic plasma jets
Grows by consuming vast amounts of interstellar gas, dust, and colliding stars

facts_and_myths.claim: The supermassive black hole TON 618 contains over 66 billion times the mass of our Sun.
facts_and_myths.explanation: TON 618 is one of the most gargantuan supermassive black holes known, weighing as much as an entire small galaxy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The diameter of TON 618's event horizon is roughly 400 billion kilometers, over 40 times the orbit of Neptune.

facts_and_myths.claim: Supermassive black holes formed recently from regular dying stars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They formed in the early universe through mechanisms still being researched, including direct collapse of primordial gas clouds.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Milky Way's supermassive black hole is named Sagittarius A* and contains 4.3 million solar masses.

name: Sagittarius A*
visual_anchor: A glowing orange-red ring of heated plasma encircling the dark silhouette of the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way.
core_traits: Supermassive black hole anchoring the exact rotational center of the Milky Way galaxy
Located approximately 26,000 light-years away from Earth in the constellation Sagittarius
Has an estimated mass equivalent to 4.3 million solar masses
Directly photographed by the Event Horizon Telescope collaboration and revealed in May 2022

facts_and_myths.claim: Reinhard Genzel and Andrea Ghez won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics for tracking stars orbiting Sagittarius A*.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They spent decades measuring the rapid orbital motion of star S2, proving beyond doubt a 4-million-solar-mass supermassive compact object sits there.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Star S2 whips around Sagittarius A* at speeds exceeding 7,000 kilometers per second (nearly 3% the speed of light).

facts_and_myths.claim: Sagittarius A* is actively devouring the Earth and will consume us next year.
facts_and_myths.explanation: At 26,000 light-years away, Earth is in a completely stable, safe galactic orbit around the galactic center.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The asterisk in the name was added by Robert Brown in 1982 because excited atoms are marked with asterisks in physics.

name: Event Horizon
visual_anchor: The razor-sharp spherical perimeter of utter blackness where brilliant swirling accretion light vanishes forever into a black hole.
core_traits: Boundary surrounding a black hole beyond which nothing, including light, can escape
The escape velocity at the event horizon exactly equals the speed of light
Size is defined for a non-rotating black hole by the Schwarzschild radius
Acts as a one-way causal membrane where future light cones point inexorably inward toward the singularity

facts_and_myths.claim: An astronaut falling into a supermassive black hole would pass through the event horizon without feeling anything unusual initially.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because supermassive black holes have immense event horizons, tidal gravity differences across a human body at the boundary are gentle.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: To an outside observer watching from far away, an infalling object appears to slow down and freeze at the event horizon forever due to extreme gravitational redshift.

facts_and_myths.claim: The event horizon is a hard, impenetrable physical wall made of ultra-dense matter.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is not a physical surface, but a mathematical spacetime boundary marking where escape velocity exceeds light speed.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Stephen Hawking showed that quantum fluctuations near the event horizon cause black holes to emit faint 'Hawking radiation'.

name: Gravitational Singularity
visual_anchor: An infinitely dense conceptual pinpoint at the deepest core of a black hole where the fabric of spacetime curves to infinity.
core_traits: Point of infinite density and zero volume at the very center of a black hole
Location where classical general relativity breaks down and quantum gravity effects dominate
Gravitational curvature becomes infinite, causing physical laws as currently understood to cease functioning
In rotating black holes, it is predicted to form a one-dimensional ring singularity

facts_and_myths.claim: A gravitational singularity represents a breakdown in our current mathematical equations rather than an infinite physical object.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Most theoretical physicists agree that singularities signal the need for a unified theory of quantum gravity to replace general relativity at Planck scales.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Big Bang began from an initial cosmic singularity roughly 13.8 billion years ago.

facts_and_myths.claim: Astronomers have visually seen and photographed the bare singularity inside a black hole.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Singularities are hidden behind event horizons according to the cosmic censorship hypothesis, preventing any light from revealing them.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A hypothetical singularity without an event horizon is called a 'naked singularity'.

name: Wormhole
visual_anchor: A shimmering spherical portal in deep space showing a distorted window into an entirely different galaxy millions of light-years away.
core_traits: Hypothetical topological feature of spacetime connecting two distant points across the universe
Predicted as a valid mathematical solution to Albert Einstein's field equations by Einstein and Nathan Rosen in 1935
Often conceptualized in science fiction as a shortcut enabling faster-than-light interstellar travel
Theoretical physics suggests traversable wormholes would require exotic matter with negative mass to stay open

facts_and_myths.claim: Wormholes are scientifically proven and routinely used by NASA to explore other galaxies.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Wormholes remain purely theoretical mathematical constructs; not a single real wormhole has ever been observed.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: If a wormhole existed, looking into it would resemble a crystal sphere reflecting the sky of another universe.

facts_and_myths.claim: According to general relativity, a wormhole could theoretically allow travel through both space and time.
facts_and_myths.explanation: If one mouth of a wormhole is accelerated to near light speed and returned, time dilation creates a closed timelike curve (a time machine).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Physicist Kip Thorne developed the physics of traversable wormholes for Carl Sagan's novel 'Contact'.

name: Supernova
visual_anchor: A cataclysmic stellar explosion erupting with the brilliance of an entire galaxy, scattering expanding shells of glowing heavy elements.
core_traits: Colossal, luminous explosion that marks the violent end of a massive star's life
Can briefly outshine all the hundreds of billions of stars in its host galaxy combined
Responsible for forging and dispersing heavy elements like iron, nickel, gold, and uranium across the cosmos
Leaves behind either a dense neutron star, pulsar, or black hole surrounded by an expanding nebula

facts_and_myths.claim: Virtually all the gold, silver, and heavy elements on Earth were forged inside ancient supernovae.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Nuclear fusion in dying stars and explosive nucleosynthesis in supernovae created the heavy elements that formed our planet.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: As Carl Sagan famously said, 'We are made of star-stuff.'

facts_and_myths.claim: Our Sun will end its life as a spectacular, galaxy-shattering supernova.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Sun does not have enough mass to go supernova; it will swell into a red giant and gently shed its outer layers into a planetary nebula.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In 1054 AD, Chinese astronomers documented a supernova visible in broad daylight for 23 days, creating the Crab Nebula.

name: Hypernova
visual_anchor: An unimaginably violent cosmic detonation of a giant star, blasting relativistic beams of gamma radiation from its spinning poles.
core_traits: Extremely energetic supernova that releases 10 to 100 times more energy than a standard supernova
Result of the collapse of an exceptionally massive star (over 30 solar masses) with rapid rotation
