Thought to be the primary engine driving long-duration gamma-ray bursts
Immediately forms a rapidly spinning black hole at its core

facts_and_myths.claim: A hypernova can blast beams of gamma radiation across billions of light-years that are detectable from Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The collapsar mechanism channels immense energy into narrow relativistic jets that pierce through the star into deep intergalactic space.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The term 'hypernova' was coined by astrophysicist Bohdan Paczynski in 1998.

facts_and_myths.claim: Hypernovae occur every few weeks in our own solar system.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Hypernovae are exceptionally rare across the universe, occurring only once every few hundred thousand years in an average galaxy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Eta Carinae in our galaxy is a hypergiant star considered a prime candidate for a future hypernova.

name: Milky Way Galaxy
visual_anchor: A vast barred spiral galaxy spanning 100,000 light-years, with glowing starlight arms wrapping around a golden central bulge.
core_traits: Barred spiral galaxy containing our solar system and an estimated 100 to 400 billion stars
Spans a stellar disc diameter of approximately 100,000 to 150,000 light-years
Our solar system is located in the Orion-Cygnus Arm, about 26,000 light-years from the galactic core
Part of the Local Group of galaxies alongside Andromeda and Triangulum

facts_and_myths.claim: The solar system completes one full orbit around the Milky Way center roughly once every 230 million years.
facts_and_myths.explanation: This orbital duration is known as a galactic year; when the solar system was in this current position last, dinosaurs were just emerging.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies are hurtling toward each other and will merge in about 4.5 billion years.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Milky Way is completely flat like a pristine pane of glass.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Detailed radio and infrared mapping shows the Milky Way's outer stellar disk is warped and twisted like a ruffled potato chip.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The ancient Greeks called it 'galaxias kyklos' (milky circle) from the myth of milk spilled by Hera.

name: Andromeda Galaxy
visual_anchor: A colossal spiral galaxy tilting gracefully in space, glowing with the combined light of one trillion stars across 220,000 light-years.
core_traits: Nearest major spiral galaxy to the Milky Way, located roughly 2.5 million light-years from Earth
Largest and most massive galaxy in our Local Group, containing approximately one trillion stars
Easily visible to the naked eye as a faint smudge of light on clear dark autumn nights
Approaching the Milky Way at roughly 110 kilometers per second

facts_and_myths.claim: Andromeda is the most distant permanent celestial object easily visible to the human naked eye.
facts_and_myths.explanation: At 2.5 million light-years away, the photons hitting your eye left Andromeda when early human ancestors were first walking on Earth.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: If Andromeda were brighter, it would appear six times wider than the full Moon in the night sky.

facts_and_myths.claim: When Andromeda collides with the Milky Way, planets will crash head-on into each other like cars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Distances between stars are so enormous that virtually zero individual stars will actually collide; they will slide past each other and merge into one giant elliptical galaxy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The future combined galaxy is colloquially dubbed 'Milkomeda'.

name: Triangulum Galaxy
visual_anchor: A pristine face-on spiral galaxy showing delicate cyan arms studded with sparkling pink stellar nurseries in deep space.
core_traits: Third-largest member of the Local Group of galaxies after Andromeda and the Milky Way
Located approximately 2.7 to 3 million light-years from Earth in the constellation Triangulum
Contains roughly 40 billion stars across a diameter of 60,000 light-years
Hosts NGC 604, one of the largest and most luminous star-forming H II regions known

facts_and_myths.claim: NGC 604 inside the Triangulum Galaxy is over 1,500 light-years across and contains 200 massive hot young stars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is one of the largest emission nebulae known, roughly 40 times larger than the visible portion of our Orion Nebula.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Under exceptional, pitch-black skies, M33 is the furthest naked-eye object visible without any optical aid.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Triangulum Galaxy orbits planet Jupiter.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Triangulum is an independent galaxy millions of light-years away, possibly gravitationally bound to the Andromeda Galaxy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: M33 is considered a textbook example of an unbarred spiral galaxy.

name: Large Magellanic Cloud
visual_anchor: A vibrant irregular satellite galaxy floating like a luminous celestial cloud across the starry skies of the Southern Hemisphere.
core_traits: Satellite galaxy orbiting the Milky Way, located roughly 160,000 light-years away
Fourth-largest galaxy in the Local Group, containing about 20 billion stars
Prominently visible to the naked eye from the Southern Hemisphere
Home to the Tarantula Nebula and the site of Supernova 1987A, the closest observed modern supernova

facts_and_myths.claim: Ferdinand Magellan's crew was the first group of humans ever to see the Magellanic Clouds.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Indigenous peoples of the Southern Hemisphere had observed and named them for tens of thousands of years before European exploration.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Persian astronomer Al-Sufi documented the Large Magellanic Cloud in 964 AD, calling it Al-Baqar (The White Ox).

facts_and_myths.claim: Supernova 1987A erupted in the Large Magellanic Cloud, providing astronomers their first modern supernova neutrino data.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Detected on February 23, 1987, SN 1987A was the closest observed supernova in 383 years, confirming theories of core-collapse physics.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The LMC is connected to the Small Magellanic Cloud by a bridge of gas known as the Magellanic Bridge.

name: Small Magellanic Cloud
visual_anchor: A faint hazy dwarf irregular galaxy gleaming softly beside the constellation Tucana in the deep southern night sky.
core_traits: Dwarf irregular galaxy companion to the Large Magellanic Cloud, orbiting the Milky Way
Located approximately 200,000 light-years from Earth
Contains several hundred million stars
Features the renowned bright globular cluster 47 Tucanae along its line of sight

facts_and_myths.claim: Astronomer Henrietta Swan Leavitt discovered the period-luminosity relation of Cepheid variables using stars in the SMC.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Her landmark 1912 discovery provided astronomers the first true 'standard candle' to measure distances across the universe.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Edwin Hubble used Leavitt's law to prove Andromeda was a separate galaxy outside the Milky Way.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Small Magellanic Cloud is colliding with the Moon next year.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is an external galaxy located 200,000 light-years away in deep intergalactic space.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Recent 2023 studies suggest the SMC may actually be two separate dwarf galaxies along the same line of sight.

name: Whirlpool Galaxy
visual_anchor: A breathtaking grand-design spiral galaxy sweeping majestic curving arms connected to a yellowish companion galaxy NGC 5195.
core_traits: Grand-design spiral galaxy located approximately 23 million light-years away in Canes Venatici
First galaxy classified with a recognized spiral structure, discovered by Lord Rosse in 1845
Engaged in a dramatic gravitational interaction with smaller companion galaxy NGC 5195
Renowned among amateur and professional astronomers for stunning spiral symmetry and active star formation

facts_and_myths.claim: The Whirlpool Galaxy was the first galaxy in history whose spiral structure was visually resolved.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Lord Rosse observed its spiral arms in 1845 using his 72-inch reflecting telescope, the 'Leviathan of Parsonstown'.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its prominent spiral arms are compression waves triggered by tidal interactions with its companion galaxy.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Whirlpool Galaxy is located inside the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is an external galaxy located 23 million light-years away in intergalactic space.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Three distinct supernovae have been observed in M51 between 1994 and 2011.

name: Sombrero Galaxy
visual_anchor: A brilliant golden central galactic bulge encircled by a dramatic symmetrical dark dust lane, resembling a Mexican sombrero hat.
core_traits: Lenticular or unbarred spiral galaxy located roughly 31 million light-years away in Virgo
Famous for its exceptionally bright white bulbous core and wide dark rim of absorbing dust
Resembles a traditional wide-brimmed Mexican sombrero hat seen nearly edge-on
Harbors an unusually massive central black hole of approximately 1 billion solar masses

facts_and_myths.claim: The Sombrero Galaxy possesses an enormous population of nearly 2,000 globular clusters.
facts_and_myths.explanation: This is nearly 10 times more globular clusters than the Milky Way galaxy possesses.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Vesto Slipher discovered in 1912 that M104 was moving away from Earth at 1,000 km/s, providing the first hint the universe is expanding.

facts_and_myths.claim: The dark brim of the Sombrero Galaxy is made of alien spacecraft shielding.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The dark lane consists of dense clouds of cold interstellar hydrogen gas and carbonaceous cosmic dust.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its supermassive black hole is 250 times more massive than the one at the center of our Milky Way.

name: Nebula
visual_anchor: A glowing multi-hued cloud of ionized hydrogen gas and cosmic dust glowing with neon pinks, cyans, and deep purples.
core_traits: Vast interstellar cloud of dust, hydrogen, helium, and ionized gases in outer space
Acts as a stellar nursery where gravitational collapse births new infant stars and planetary systems
Classified into emission, reflection, dark, planetary, and supernova remnant types
Illuminated either by internal newborn stars or by scattering light from nearby star systems

facts_and_myths.claim: Before the 1920s, all spiral galaxies were mistakenly called 'spiral nebulae'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Until Edwin Hubble proved galaxies were island universes millions of light-years away, astronomers assumed everything fuzzy was a nebula inside the Milky Way.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The word nebula comes directly from the Latin word for 'mist' or 'cloud'.

facts_and_myths.claim: A spaceship flying through a nebula would be enveloped in thick, blinding fog like a steam room.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Nebulae are so vacuum-sparse that inside one, you would not see fog at all; a vacuum chamber on Earth is denser than a typical nebula.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: They only appear brightly colored and opaque from billions of kilometers away due to immense optical depth.

name: Orion Nebula
visual_anchor: A swirling iridescent tapestry of glowing magenta and cyan gas sculpted by four blazing newborn stars at its heart.
core_traits: Diffuse emission and reflection nebula located in the constellation Orion just below Orion's Belt
One of the closest massive star-forming regions to Earth, located roughly 1,344 light-years away
Visible to the naked eye as the middle 'star' in Orion's sword
Illuminated and sculpted by the Trapezium Cluster, a tight group of four massive young stars

facts_and_myths.claim: The Orion Nebula is visible to the naked eye even from suburban areas with moderate light pollution.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Located in Orion's sword, it shines at apparent magnitude 4.0, appearing as a soft luminous haze through binoculars.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hubble images of M42 revealed dozens of proplyds - protoplanetary disks of dust surrounding infant stars where new planets are currently forming.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Orion Nebula is the remnant of an exploding star that blew up last century.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is an active stellar nursery birthing stars, not a supernova remnant like the Crab Nebula.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It measures approximately 24 light-years across and contains enough material to produce 2,000 suns.

name: Crab Nebula
visual_anchor: An intricate web of tangled red and orange filaments of ionized gas expanding outward from a rapidly pulsing central star.
core_traits: Supernova remnant located in the constellation Taurus, approximately 6,500 light-years away
Result of a historic supernova witnessed and recorded by Chinese, Japanese, and Arab astronomers in 1054 AD
At its center spins the Crab Pulsar, a neutron star rotating 30 times per second
First entry in Charles Messier's famous 1774 catalog of non-comet deep sky objects (M1)

facts_and_myths.claim: The supernova that created the Crab Nebula was so bright in 1054 AD that people could read books by its light at night.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Historical chronicles recorded that SN 1054 was four times brighter than Venus, visible in broad daylight for 23 days and at night for two years.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Crab Pulsar emits beams of radiation across the entire electromagnetic spectrum from radio to gamma rays.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Crab Nebula is named because it is inhabited by giant extraterrestrial space crabs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It was named by the Earl of Rosse in 1844 because his initial telescope sketch resembled the shape of a horseshoe crab.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The gas filaments are expanding into space at over 1,500 kilometers per second.

name: Eagle Nebula
visual_anchor: A colossal glowing interstellar cloud crowned by towering dark spires of cold gas and dust birthing new stars.
core_traits: Young open cluster of stars embedded in a diffuse emission nebula in the constellation Serpens
Located approximately 7,000 light-years from Earth
World-famous for housing the 'Pillars of Creation', monumental columns of gas and dust
Actively sculpted by fierce stellar winds and ultraviolet radiation from hot young O and B stars

facts_and_myths.claim: The iconic Hubble Space Telescope photograph taken in 1995 made the Eagle Nebula famous worldwide.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Jeff Hester and Paul Scowen's 'Pillars of Creation' photo is widely considered one of the most famous astronomical images ever taken.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The James Webb Space Telescope imaged the nebula in 2022 in infrared, revealing thousands of stars hidden inside the pillars.

facts_and_myths.claim: The pillars inside the Eagle Nebula are only a few meters tall.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The tallest pillar is approximately 4 to 5 light-years tall, roughly the distance from our Sun to the nearest star Proxima Centauri.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dense pockets of gas at the tips of the pillars called EGGs (evaporating gaseous globules) contain embryonic stars.

name: Ring Nebula
visual_anchor: A perfect glowing oval ring of rainbow-colored gas surrounding a solitary dying white dwarf star in Lyra.
core_traits: Textbook planetary nebula located in the northern constellation Lyra, roughly 2,570 light-years away
Formed when a dying medium-mass star expelled its outer layers of ionized gas thousands of years ago
Features a central white dwarf star that illuminates the expanding shell of gas
Displays concentric rings of blue ionized helium, green oxygen, and red nitrogen gas

facts_and_myths.claim: Planetary nebulae like the Ring Nebula are made of giant solid rocky planets.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Early astronomers using primitive telescopes thought their round greenish disks looked like Uranus, so they misnamed them 'planetary nebulae'.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Ring Nebula is actually barrel-shaped, but appears like a ring because Earth is looking straight down its central axis.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Ring Nebula provides a direct preview of what our Sun will look like when it dies in 5 billion years.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Like M57's central star, our Sun will cast off its outer envelopes and leave behind a cooling white dwarf inside a glowing gas shell.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The ring is expanding into space at about 20 to 30 kilometers per second.

name: Helix Nebula
visual_anchor: A titanic glowing celestial iris of turquoise and crimson gas staring out from deep space like a colossal cosmic eye.
core_traits: One of the closest planetary nebulae to Earth, located roughly 655 light-years away in Aquarius
Spans nearly 3 light-years across, formed by a dying Sun-like star shedding its outer layers
Earned the popular internet nickname 'Eye of God' due to its striking resemblance to a human eye
Contains thousands of cometary knots - dense globules of gas trailing gaseous tails outward

facts_and_myths.claim: The Helix Nebula is widely known in popular culture as the 'Eye of God'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: High-resolution photos showing its blue pupil-like core surrounded by red eyelids led to viral internet fame.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The nebula's central white dwarf is so hot (120,000 degrees Celsius) that it floods the surrounding gas with intense ultraviolet light.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Helix Nebula was artificially created by human satellite lasers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is a natural planetary nebula formed over 10,000 years ago by natural stellar evolutionary processes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It was discovered by German astronomer Karl Ludwig Harding before 1824.

name: Horsehead Nebula
visual_anchor: A dramatic black silhouette of a horse's head carved from dark cosmic dust, rearing against a radiant curtain of crimson hydrogen gas.
core_traits: Small dark nebula located in the constellation Orion just south of the star Alnitak
Located approximately 1,375 light-years from Earth
Appears as the stark silhouette of a horse's head against the glowing reddish emission nebula IC 434
Discovered in 1888 by Scottish-American astronomer Williamina Fleming on a photographic plate

facts_and_myths.claim: The Horsehead Nebula was discovered by a pioneering female astronomer named Williamina Fleming.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Fleming was one of the famed 'Harvard Computers' who analyzed glass photographic plates, cataloging it in 1888.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The nebula appears bright red only in long-exposure photography; through an eyepiece it is notoriously difficult to detect.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Horsehead Nebula will remain in the shape of a horse forever.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Radiation and fierce stellar winds from nearby hot stars are eroding the dust cloud; it will completely disperse in about 5 million years.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The dark dust consists of microscopic carbon grains and complex polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons.

name: Carina Nebula
visual_anchor: A colossal, tempestuous cloud of glowing stellar gas four times larger than the Orion Nebula, hosting the hypergiant Eta Carinae.
core_traits: Immense bright emission nebula in the southern constellation Carina, located roughly 8,500 light-years away
One of the largest diffuse nebulae in our galaxy, spanning approximately 300 light-years across
Home to Eta Carinae, one of the most luminous, unstable hypergiant stars known
Features spectacular features including the Keyhole Nebula and the Homunculus Nebula

facts_and_myths.claim: The Carina Nebula is significantly larger and more luminous than the famous Orion Nebula.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is roughly four times larger and far more luminous, but less widely known because it is only visible from the Southern Hemisphere.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The James Webb Space Telescope's famous 'Cosmic Cliffs' photograph captured star-forming ridges inside the Carina Nebula.

facts_and_myths.claim: Eta Carinae inside the nebula is a completely stable star that will live for trillions of years.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Eta Carinae is violently unstable and could detonate in a supernova or hypernova at any moment in cosmological time.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: During its Great Eruption in 1843, Eta Carinae briefly became the second-brightest star in Earth's entire night sky.

name: Tarantula Nebula
visual_anchor: A gargantuan star-forming region of spidery glowing gas filaments spanning 1,000 light-years in the Large Magellanic Cloud.
core_traits: Extremely luminous H II star-forming region located in the Large Magellanic Cloud, 160,000 light-years away
Most active and largest starburst region known in the entire Local Group of galaxies
If it were at the distance of the Orion Nebula, it would cover 60 full Moons and cast shadows on Earth at night
Contains star cluster R136, home to R136a1, one of the most massive stars ever discovered (over 200 solar masses)

facts_and_myths.claim: If the Tarantula Nebula were as close to Earth as the Orion Nebula, it would cast visible shadows on the ground at night.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its sheer scale (1,000 light-years across) and immense luminosity would make it shine brighter than the full Moon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It was named the Tarantula Nebula because its tangled glowing gas filaments resemble the hairy legs of a giant spider.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Tarantula Nebula is inside our solar system.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It resides in an entirely separate satellite galaxy, the Large Magellanic Cloud, 160,000 light-years away.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Supernova 1987A occurred on the outskirts of the Tarantula Nebula.

name: Cat's Eye Nebula
visual_anchor: An astonishingly intricate layered planetary nebula with concentric rings, gas knots, and intertwining loops glowing like a green feline eye.
core_traits: Complex planetary nebula in the northern constellation Draco, located roughly 3,300 light-years away
One of the most structurally intricate nebulae known, displaying concentric shells, jets, and knotted gas arcs
First planetary nebula whose spectrum was analyzed by William Huggins in 1864, proving nebulae are made of hot gas
Formed by pulses and stellar wind ejections from a dying binary central star system

facts_and_myths.claim: William Huggins's 1864 observation of the Cat's Eye Nebula proved that nebulae were made of glowing gas rather than unresolved distant stars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its spectrum showed discrete bright emission lines characteristic of a rarefied glowing gas rather than a continuous stellar spectrum.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hubble images revealed 11 or more concentric nested rings blown out like smoke rings every 1,500 years.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Cat's Eye Nebula is shaped by the paws of an enormous cosmic cat.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its complex symmetrical concentric patterns are driven by a binary star pair ejecting periodic pulses of magnetic stellar winds.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The central star is 10,000 times more luminous than our Sun.

name: Butterfly Nebula
visual_anchor: Two colossal sweeping wings of glowing white and violet gas stretching across space like a celestial butterfly spreading its wings.
core_traits: Bipolar planetary nebula in the constellation Scorpius, roughly 3,800 light-years from Earth
Displays two vast delicate wings of superheated gas expanding outward from a dying central star
Has one of the hottest central stars known, with a surface temperature exceeding 250,000 degrees Celsius
The central star is hidden behind a dark equatorial donut of dense cosmic dust

facts_and_myths.claim: The central star of the Butterfly Nebula is over 30 times hotter than the surface of our Sun.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With a surface temperature around 250,000 degrees Celsius, it is one of the hottest known stars in the entire Milky Way galaxy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The wings of gas are expanding into space at over 1 million kilometers per hour.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Butterfly Nebula is made of organic living butterfly wings.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is composed of incandescent plasma, ionized nitrogen, hydrogen, and mineral dust grains ejected by a dying white dwarf.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The nebula spans over three light-years from wingtip to wingtip.

name: Pillars of Creation
visual_anchor: Towering monolithic fingers of dark interstellar gas and dust bathed in the eerie green and blue glow of newborn starlight.
core_traits: Famous astronomical formation of elephant trunks of interstellar gas and dust in the Eagle Nebula (M16)
Located approximately 7,000 light-years away from Earth in the constellation Serpens
Captured in an iconic 1995 Hubble Space Telescope photograph that became a global cultural icon
Serve as active incubators where gravity condenses gas to birth brand-new stars

facts_and_myths.claim: The tallest pillar in the Pillars of Creation is roughly four light-years from base to tip.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The left pillar is about four to five light-years long, approximately the same distance from our Sun to Alpha Centauri.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In 2022, the James Webb Space Telescope imaged the Pillars in near-infrared, making the dust transparent to show thousands of sparkling orange protostars.

facts_and_myths.claim: A nearby supernova completely destroyed the Pillars of Creation thousands of years ago.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Earlier infrared studies hypothesized a supernova shockwave had destroyed them, but newer Spitzer and Webb data showed the pillars remain structurally intact.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The photo was chosen by Time magazine as one of the 100 most influential images of all time.

name: White Dwarf
visual_anchor: An intensely glowing blue-white compact stellar corpse the size of Earth gleaming amid darkness, supported by electron degeneracy pressure.
core_traits: Stellar core remnant left behind after a low-to-medium mass star sheds its outer envelopes
Extremely dense: packs roughly the mass of the Sun into a volume approximately the size of Earth
Supported against further gravitational collapse exclusively by electron degeneracy pressure
The ultimate evolutionary fate of over 97% of all stars in the Milky Way, including our Sun

facts_and_myths.claim: A single teaspoon of white dwarf material would weigh as much as an elephant on Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With a density of roughly 1,000,000 grams per cubic centimeter, a teaspoon weighs about 5 metric tons (roughly the weight of an elephant).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sirius B, orbiting the brightest star in our night sky, was the first white dwarf star ever discovered.

facts_and_myths.claim: White dwarfs generate energy through continuous nuclear fusion in their cores.
facts_and_myths.explanation: White dwarfs have exhausted all nuclear fuel; they shine purely from residual thermal heat left over from their stellar life.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Given trillions of years, a white dwarf will eventually cool into a cold, dark 'black dwarf' (none exist yet in our young universe).

name: Red Giant
visual_anchor: A gargantuan, pulsating ruddy-orange star billowing glowing atmospheric layers into space as its core contracts.
core_traits: Luminous giant star in a late stage of stellar evolution that has exhausted hydrogen fuel in its core
Expands to hundreds of times its original radius while its surface temperature cools to a reddish hue
Burns hydrogen in a shell surrounding an inert helium core
Our Sun will expand into a red giant in approximately 5 billion years, engulfing Mercury and Venus

facts_and_myths.claim: When the Sun becomes a red giant, it will expand large enough to swallow the inner planets.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Sun's outer atmosphere will expand past Mercury and Venus, and likely engulf Earth or leave its surface molten.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Aldebaran, the eye of the constellation Taurus, is a prominent red giant located 65 light-years away.

facts_and_myths.claim: Red giants are hotter on their surface than blue stars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because a red giant's immense energy is spread over an enormous surface area, its surface cools to roughly 3,000 Kelvin, giving it a red color.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Despite their gigantic size, the outer atmospheres of red giants are extremely tenuous and rarefied.

name: Red Supergiant
visual_anchor: A monstrous crimson star pulsating violently, so enormous that its outer envelope would reach the orbit of Jupiter.
core_traits: Largest stars in the universe in terms of physical volume and diameter
Evolved from massive stars (over 10 to 40 solar masses) that have exhausted core hydrogen fuel
Can span radii over 1,000 times that of the Sun (e.g., Betelgeuse, Antares, UY Scuti)
Destined to die in a catastrophic core-collapse Type II supernova explosion

facts_and_myths.claim: If the red supergiant Betelgeuse were placed at the center of our solar system, its surface would extend past Mars and Jupiter.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With a diameter roughly 700 to 1,000 times that of our Sun, it would swallow Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, and possibly Jupiter.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Betelgeuse experienced the 'Great Dimming' in late 2019 when it sneezed out a giant cloud of obscuring dust.

facts_and_myths.claim: Red supergiants live for hundreds of billions of years.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because they burn their nuclear fuel at furious rates, massive stars live very fast and die young, lasting only a few million years.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Inside a red supergiant, progressive shell fusion creates an 'onion skin' of elements ending in an iron core.

name: Blue Supergiant
visual_anchor: A blazing sapphire-blue mega-star radiating blistering ultraviolet light and ferocious stellar winds into surrounding space.
core_traits: Extremely hot and luminous supergiant star of spectral class O or B
Surface temperatures range from 10,000 to over 50,000 Kelvin, giving them a brilliant blue-white glow
Tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of times more luminous than our Sun
Famous examples include Rigel in Orion and Deneb in Cygnus

facts_and_myths.claim: Rigel in Orion shines with the luminosity of over 100,000 Suns.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Rigel is a blue supergiant roughly 860 light-years away whose blinding output makes it the seventh brightest star in our night sky.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Because they burn through hydrogen fuel furiously, blue supergiants have lifetimes of only a few million to tens of millions of years.

facts_and_myths.claim: Blue stars are cooler than red stars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In physics and astronomy, blue light corresponds to higher energy and hotter temperatures; blue stars are vastly hotter than red stars.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Blue supergiants can fluctuate back and forth into red supergiants during late-stage burning phases.

name: Neutron Star
visual_anchor: A city-sized ultra-dense sphere spinning in the void, wrapped in crushing gravity and crackling with magnetic fields.
core_traits: Collapsed core of a massive supergiant star formed during a supernova explosion
Packs roughly 1.4 to 2.1 solar masses into a sphere only about 20 kilometers in diameter
Composed almost entirely of tightly packed neutrons supported by neutron degeneracy pressure
Possesses extreme surface gravity roughly 200 billion times greater than Earth's

facts_and_myths.claim: A single teaspoon of matter from a neutron star would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Atomic nuclei are crushed together without empty space, reaching densities of 100 trillion grams per cubic centimeter (as heavy as Mount Everest).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The crust of a neutron star is composed of 'nuclear pasta', the strongest material known in the universe.

facts_and_myths.claim: Neutron stars are as large as planets like Jupiter.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A neutron star would comfortably fit inside the boundaries of a modern city like New York, London, or Tokyo.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Colliding neutron stars (kilonovae) produce massive amounts of gold, platinum, and radioactive heavy elements.

name: Pulsar
visual_anchor: A rapidly spinning neutron star sweeping twin blinding beams of electromagnetic radiation across space like a cosmic lighthouse.
core_traits: Highly magnetized, rotating neutron star that emits beams of electromagnetic radiation from its magnetic poles
Observed as rhythmic, periodic pulses when the beam sweeps across Earth's line of sight
Can rotate from several times per second up to hundreds of times per second (millisecond pulsars)
Discovered in 1967 by Jocelyn Bell Burnell using a radio telescope

facts_and_myths.claim: When Jocelyn Bell Burnell first discovered pulsar signals, astronomers humorously labeled them 'LGM-1' for Little Green Men.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The pulses were so eerily precise and rapid (every 1.33 seconds) that scientists initially considered extraterrestrial artificial signals.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The fastest known millisecond pulsar, PSR J1748-2446ad, spins at an astonishing 716 times per second.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pulsars emit pulses because the star physically turns on and off like a blinking light bulb.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The beams are continuously active; the pulsing appearance is caused by the star's rapid rotation sweeping the beam past our vantage point.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Millisecond pulsars are so stable that they rival the accuracy of atomic clocks on Earth.

name: Magnetar
visual_anchor: An ultra-magnetic neutron star surrounded by distorted quantum vacuum fields, erupting with high-energy gamma-ray starquakes.
core_traits: Type of neutron star possessing an extremely powerful magnetic field up to a quadrillion Gauss
Has the strongest magnetic fields measured in the universe, a thousand times stronger than typical neutron stars
Experiences 'starquakes' where its rigid crust cracks, releasing massive blasts of X-rays and gamma rays
Magnetic field is strong enough to dissolve atoms and wipe credit cards from halfway to the Moon

facts_and_myths.claim: A magnetar passing within 1,000 kilometers of Earth would literally dissolve human bodies at an atomic level.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its magnetic field would distort atomic electron clouds into needle-like cylinders, instantly destroying all molecular chemistry.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In December 2004, a giant flare from magnetar SGR 1806-20 (50,000 light-years away) visibly altered Earth's upper ionosphere.

facts_and_myths.claim: Magnetars live for hundreds of billions of years in an active high-magnetic state.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their extreme magnetic fields decay rapidly through magnetic field dissipation, lasting only about 10,000 years in peak active phase.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Only around 30 confirmed magnetars are known in the entire Milky Way.

name: Quasar
visual_anchor: A blinding beacon at the edge of the observable universe powered by a supermassive black hole consuming gas in a brilliant accretion blaze.
core_traits: Extremely luminous active galactic nucleus powered by a supermassive black hole accreting matter
Can shine thousands of times brighter than an entire galaxy of hundreds of billions of stars
Located at immense cosmological distances, seen as they existed in the early universe billions of years ago
Releases titanic amounts of energy across radio, optical, ultraviolet, and X-ray wavelengths

facts_and_myths.claim: The most luminous quasars shine brighter than 100 trillion Suns.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Frictional and gravitational energy in their accretion disks converts falling matter into radiant energy with extraordinary efficiency.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The word quasar is a contraction of 'quasi-stellar radio source' because they initially looked like stars through optical telescopes.

facts_and_myths.claim: Quasars are individual giant stars located in our neighboring solar neighborhood.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They are the active cores of ancient baby galaxies billions of light-years away, powered by supermassive black holes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Quasar J0529-4351 discovered in 2024 consumes the mass equivalent of one entire Sun every single day.

name: Blazar
visual_anchor: A supermassive black hole firing an intense relativistic plasma jet pointed directly down the line of sight toward Earth.
core_traits: Active galactic nucleus with a relativistic jet pointed almost directly toward the observer on Earth
Special orientation causes relativistic beaming, amplifying perceived brightness and variability
Displays rapid fluctuations in brightness over days, hours, or minutes
Source of high-energy cosmic neutrinos and ultra-high-energy gamma rays

facts_and_myths.claim: The difference between a quasar and a blazar is primarily the angle at which Earth views its jet.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Under the unified model of active galactic nuclei, a blazar is simply a quasar whose particle jet is pointing directly down Earth's throat.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In 2017, the IceCube Neutrino Observatory traced a high-energy cosmic neutrino back to blazar TXS 0506+056.

facts_and_myths.claim: Blazar jets travel at 1,000 times the speed of light.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The jet particles travel at 99.9% the speed of light; optical illusion effects cause 'apparent superluminal motion', but no physical matter exceeds light speed.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Blazars are among the most violent particle accelerators in the universe.

name: Cosmic Microwave Background
visual_anchor: A speckled oval cosmological heat map showing tiny temperature fluctuations across the infant universe 380,000 years after the Big Bang.
core_traits: Electromagnetic radiation left over from the earliest stage of the universe, often called the 'afterglow of the Big Bang'
Formed during the epoch of recombination roughly 380,000 years after the Big Bang when the universe became transparent
Permeates all of space uniformly at an average temperature of approximately 2.725 Kelvin (-270.4 degrees Celsius)
Discovered accidentally in 1965 by Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson, earning them the Nobel Prize

facts_and_myths.claim: A small fraction of static 'snow' on old analog television sets was caused by the Cosmic Microwave Background.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Roughly 1% of the static interference on untuned analog rabbit-ear televisions was direct interaction with CMB photons.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Tiny temperature variations of one part in 100,000 in the CMB represent the primordial seeds that grew into all galaxies.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Cosmic Microwave Background originated from stars burning in the Milky Way.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The CMB was created billions of years before any stars, galaxies, or planets existed in the cosmos.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Penzias and Wilson initially thought the hiss in their antenna was caused by pigeon droppings inside the horn.

name: Dark Matter
visual_anchor: A vast invisible cosmic web whose immense gravitational pull bends light and anchors glowing galaxies across space.
core_traits: Hypothetical form of matter that does not interact with electromagnetic radiation, making it completely invisible
Accounts for approximately 85% of all matter in the universe and 27% of its total mass-energy
Inferred through its gravitational effects on galactic rotation curves and gravitational lensing
Forms an invisible halo around galaxies that prevents them from flying apart as they spin

facts_and_myths.claim: Vera Rubin confirmed dark matter by discovering that stars on the outer edges of spiral galaxies orbit just as fast as stars near the center.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Under Newtonian gravity, outer stars should move slower; their high speeds proved an unseen halo of dark matter encloses galaxies.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Bullet Cluster provides compelling visual proof of dark matter, showing gravitational mass separated from normal X-ray gas during a galaxy collision.

facts_and_myths.claim: Dark matter and antimatter are the exact same thing.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Antimatter interacts normally with light and annihilates on contact with normal matter; dark matter does not interact with light at all.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Scientists still do not know what particle makes up dark matter, with WIMPs and axions being leading candidates.

name: Dark Energy
visual_anchor: An enigmatic repulsive force stretching the dark fabric of space, accelerating the expansion of galaxies away from each other.
core_traits: Mysterious form of energy that permeates all space and accelerates the expansion of the universe
Accounts for roughly 68% of the total energy and mass of the entire universe
Discovered in 1998 through observations of distant Type Ia supernovae by two independent research teams
Acts as a repulsive cosmic pressure counteracting gravitational attraction on cosmological scales

facts_and_myths.claim: Astronomers discovered dark energy by realizing the expansion of the universe is speeding up, not slowing down.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Measurements of distant Type Ia supernovae showed they were fainter than expected, proving cosmic expansion has been accelerating for 5 billion years.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The discovery earned Saul Perlmutter, Brian Schmidt, and Adam Riess the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics.

facts_and_myths.claim: Dark energy can be mined and used to power cars and smartphones today.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Dark energy density is incredibly diffuse (about 10^-29 g/cm3), only having noticeable effects across vast intergalactic voids.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Albert Einstein originally introduced the 'Cosmological Constant' to keep the universe static, later calling it his 'biggest blunder'.

name: Gravitational Wave
visual_anchor: Concentric rippling distortions in the fabric of grid-like spacetime radiating outward from two colliding black holes.
core_traits: Invisible ripples in the fabric of spacetime that travel at the speed of light
Generated by some of the most violent and energetic processes in the universe, such as colliding black holes or neutron stars
Predicted by Albert Einstein in 1916 as a consequence of his general theory of relativity
First directly detected on September 14, 2015, by the LIGO interferometers from a binary black hole merger

facts_and_myths.claim: LIGO's first detection of gravitational waves measured a spacetime ripple smaller than one ten-thousandth the width of a proton.
facts_and_myths.explanation: LIGO's laser interferometers detected a length change across 4-kilometer arms of less than 10^-18 meters.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Rainer Weiss, Kip Thorne, and Barry Barish were awarded the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics for the historic breakthrough.

facts_and_myths.claim: Gravitational waves are sound waves traveling through air.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They are distortions in spacetime itself that travel freely through the total vacuum of space at the speed of light.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: When converted to audio frequencies, the final collision of two black holes makes a characteristic rising 'chirp' sound.

name: Light-Year
visual_anchor: A ray of golden light traversing a vast cosmic expanse of interstellar void studded with distant pinpoints of stars.
core_traits: Unit of astronomical distance equal to the distance that light travels in a vacuum in one Julian year
Equivalent to approximately 9.46 trillion kilometers (5.88 trillion miles) or 63,241 Astronomical Units
Used primarily to express distances to stars and other objects on an interstellar or galactic scale
Looking at an object one light-year away means seeing it as it looked one year in the past

facts_and_myths.claim: A light-year is a unit of time measuring how long an astronomical year takes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Despite containing the word 'year', a light-year measures physical distance, not elapsed time.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Looking through a telescope at Andromeda (2.5 million light-years away) is looking 2.5 million years into the past.

facts_and_myths.claim: It takes light just over 4 years to travel from Earth to the nearest star system, Alpha Centauri.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Proxima Centauri is located roughly 4.24 light-years from our solar system.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A typical commercial airliner traveling at 900 km/h would take over 1.2 million years to travel just one single light-year.

name: Parsec
visual_anchor: A geometric triangle spanning Earth's orbit and a distant star, demonstrating the tiny parallax angle of one arcsecond.
core_traits: Unit of distance used in astronomy, defined as the distance at which one AU subtends an angle of one arcsecond
Equivalent to approximately 3.26 light-years or 30.9 trillion kilometers
Derived from the combination of 'parallax' and 'arcsecond'
Standard unit preferred by professional astrophysicists and astronomers over light-years

facts_and_myths.claim: Han Solo famously bragged that the Millennium Falcon made the Kessel Run in less than twelve parsecs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The famous Star Wars quote initially sounded like a mistake using distance for time, later retconned as taking a dangerous shorter spatial route.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: One kiloparsec (kpc) is 1,000 parsecs, and one megaparsec (Mpc) is 1,000,000 parsecs, used for measuring intergalactic distances.

facts_and_myths.claim: A parsec is shorter than a light-year.
facts_and_myths.explanation: One parsec equals approximately 3.26 light-years, making it more than three times longer than a single light-year.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The parallax method to determine stellar distance in parsecs was first successfully achieved by Friedrich Bessel in 1838 for 61 Cygni.

name: Exoplanet
visual_anchor: A foreign alien planet with purple oceans and twin moons orbiting in front of an alien red dwarf star.
core_traits: Planet that orbits a star outside our solar system
Thousands of confirmed exoplanets discovered using transit photometry and radial velocity methods
Include diverse planetary archetypes such as Hot Jupiters, Super-Earths, mini-Neptunes, and water worlds
First confirmed discovery around a Sun-like star was 51 Pegasi b in 1995 by Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz

facts_and_myths.claim: NASA's Kepler and TESS space telescopes discovered that there are more planets than stars in our galaxy.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Statistical data confirms that almost every star in the Milky Way hosts at least one planet on average.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The habitable zone around a star where liquid water can pool is nicknamed the 'Goldilocks Zone'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Astronomers have physically landed human rovers on confirmed exoplanets.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Exoplanets are trillions of kilometers away in other star systems; all study is done through telescopes and spectroscopy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: 55 Cancri e is a carbon-rich Super-Earth thought to have an interior composed largely of diamond.

name: Super-Earth
visual_anchor: A massive rocky alien planet with deep blue oceans and towering mountain ridges orbiting close to an orange star.
core_traits: Extrasolar planet with a mass higher than Earth's but substantially below that of ice giants Uranus and Neptune
Typically defined as having 1.5 to 10 times the mass of Earth
May possess thick atmospheres, global water oceans, or intense volcanic geology
One of the most common types of exoplanets found in the Milky Way, despite being absent in our own solar system

facts_and_myths.claim: Super-Earths are extremely common across our galaxy even though our solar system has none.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Exoplanet surveys reveal Super-Earths and mini-Neptunes are the most abundant planet types around Milky Way stars.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: LHS 1140 b is a rocky Super-Earth in the habitable zone of a red dwarf that is a prime candidate for atmospheric study.

facts_and_myths.claim: The name 'Super-Earth' guarantees the planet has breathable air, trees, and intelligent civilizations.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The term refers purely to physical mass and size, with no implication regarding temperature, habitability, or life.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Due to high surface gravity, mountains on a rocky Super-Earth would be shorter and atmospheric pressure could be crushing.

name: Hot Jupiter
visual_anchor: A colossal gas giant glowing dull cherry-red, skimming perilously close over the churning surface of its parent star.
core_traits: Class of gas giant exoplanets that are physically similar to Jupiter but have very short orbital periods
Orbit extremely close to their parent stars (often inside 0.05 AU), taking only a few days or hours to complete a year
Subjected to blistering stellar radiation, driving atmospheric temperatures well above 1,000 degrees Celsius
51 Pegasi b was the first Hot Jupiter ever discovered in 1995

facts_and_myths.claim: On the Hot Jupiter WASP-76b, temperatures are so extreme that it rains molten iron from the sky.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Daytime temperatures exceed 2,400 degrees Celsius vaporizing iron, which winds blow to the cooler nightside where it condenses and rains liquid iron droplets.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hot Jupiters are tidally locked, meaning one face suffers perpetual searing day while the other faces eternal night.

facts_and_myths.claim: Hot Jupiters formed in the exact scorching orbits where they currently reside.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Standard models show gas giants cannot form that close to a star; they formed in cold outer regions and migrated inward through gravitational drag.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some Hot Jupiters have atmospheres so puffed up by heat that their density is lower than styrofoam.

name: Rogue Planet
visual_anchor: A lonely frozen terrestrial world adrift in the pitch-black void between star systems without any parent sun.
core_traits: Planetary-mass object that orbits the galactic center directly rather than orbiting a host star
Ejected from its original planetary system during chaotic gravitational interactions among early sibling planets
Wanders through the freezing darkness of interstellar space alone
Detected via gravitational microlensing when its mass briefly magnifies light from a background star

facts_and_myths.claim: Astronomers estimate there may be billions more rogue planets wandering the Milky Way than stars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Simulations and microlensing surveys suggest hundreds of billions of ejected rogue worlds drift freely across our galaxy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Despite having no sun, a rogue planet could theoretically retain geothermal heat and support liquid subsurface oceans insulated by thick ice.

facts_and_myths.claim: A rogue planet is entering the solar system to destroy Earth next Tuesday.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Interstellar space is vast, and no rogue planets have been detected on any collision or close-encounter trajectory with our solar system.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will discover thousands of rogue planets using wide-field infrared microlensing.

name: Brown Dwarf
visual_anchor: A massive glowing magenta sphere with swirling storm stripes, hovering ambiguously between a giant planet and a dim star.
core_traits: Substellar object that is more massive than the heaviest gas giant planets but below the minimum mass needed for hydrogen fusion
Ranges from roughly 13 to 80 Jupiter masses
Can fuse deuterium and sometimes lithium during their early lives, but never ignite stable hydrogen fusion
Often referred to popularly as 'failed stars'

facts_and_myths.claim: Brown dwarfs are actually reddish-brown or magenta in color rather than chocolate brown.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They emit most of their light in the infrared; their visual appearance ranges from deep red to dark magenta depending on temperature.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Luhman 16 binary system contains two brown dwarfs located just 6.5 light-years from Earth, our third closest star system.

facts_and_myths.claim: Brown dwarfs are solid rock and iron like planet Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Brown dwarfs are composed almost entirely of hydrogen and helium gas, resembling an oversized Jupiter.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Cool brown dwarfs can have atmospheric clouds made of liquid iron, silicate sand, and ruby-sapphire minerals.

name: Accretion Disk
visual_anchor: A blinding, flattened vortex of glowing gas and dust spiraling at relativistic speeds into the maw of a central black hole.
core_traits: Structure formed by diffuse material in orbital motion around a massive central body (black hole, neutron star, or newborn star)
Gravitational and frictional forces compress and heat the swirling material to millions of degrees
Emits powerful electromagnetic radiation, often predominantly in X-ray and ultraviolet wavelengths
One of the most efficient energy conversion mechanisms in the universe, turning up to 40% of rest mass into radiation

facts_and_myths.claim: An accretion disk around a spinning black hole converts mass into energy vastly more efficiently than nuclear fusion.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Nuclear fusion converts about 0.7% of mass to energy, while a spinning Kerr black hole's accretion disk can convert up to 42% into radiation.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Doppler effect makes the side of the disk rotating toward Earth appear significantly brighter than the side moving away.

facts_and_myths.claim: Accretion disks only exist around black holes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Accretion disks also form around white dwarfs in cataclysmic variables, neutron stars, and newborn protostars during planet formation.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Magnetic fields in accretion disks twist into coils that launch relativistic plasma jets from their poles.

name: Cosmic Ray
visual_anchor: Subatomic protons and atomic nuclei blazing through the interstellar void at 99.9% the speed of light.
core_traits: High-energy protons and atomic nuclei that move through space at nearly the speed of light
Originate from supernovae explosions, active galactic nuclei, and colliding stars across the galaxy
Collide with Earth's upper atmosphere, producing secondary showers of muons, electrons, and pions
Pose a major radiation hazard to astronauts in deep space beyond Earth's protective magnetic field

facts_and_myths.claim: Apollo astronauts reported seeing strange bright flashes of light in their eyes while resting in deep space.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cosmic rays traveling through their eyeballs passed through the retina, emitting Cherenkov radiation that produced perceived flashes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The 'Oh-My-God particle' detected in Utah in 1991 had so much kinetic energy (3x10^20 eV) that a single subatomic proton packed the punch of a fast-pitch baseball.

facts_and_myths.claim: Cosmic rays are beams of visible laser light.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Despite the historical name 'ray', they are physical matter - individual atomic nuclei, mostly protons and helium cores.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Victor Hess discovered cosmic rays in 1912 by taking electroscopes up in high-altitude hot air balloons, winning the 1936 Nobel Prize.

name: Gamma-Ray Burst
visual_anchor: A hyper-energetic blinding beam of emerald-blue gamma radiation stabbing across billions of light-years of intergalactic space.
core_traits: Most energetic electromagnetic explosions in the universe since the Big Bang
Short-duration bursts are caused by colliding neutron stars, while long bursts are caused by hypernovae collapsing into black holes
Releases more energy in a few seconds than the Sun will produce in its entire 10-billion-year lifespan
Beams out in narrow relativistic jets focused along the rotational axis of the dying progenitor

facts_and_myths.claim: A nearby gamma-ray burst aimed directly at Earth could strip our ozone layer and trigger a mass extinction.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A GRB within a few thousand light-years would flood Earth with nitrogen oxides, destroying the ozone shield and causing global ultraviolet sterilizing radiation.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Some paleontologists hypothesize the Late Ordovician mass extinction 445 million years ago was caused by a GRB.

facts_and_myths.claim: Gamma-ray bursts were discovered by astronomers searching for alien communications.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They were discovered in 1967 by American Vela satellites designed to spy on secret Soviet atmospheric nuclear bomb tests.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: GRBs occur roughly once per day across the observable universe.

name: Polaris
visual_anchor: A solitary bright star shining motionless at the exact zenith of a swirling circular time-lapse of northern star trails.
core_traits: Current northern pole star located in the constellation Ursa Minor
Marks the true north celestial pole, remaining virtually stationary in the sky as Earth rotates
Used for centuries by northern navigators, explorers, and sailors to determine latitude
Multiple star system located approximately 433 light-years from Earth

facts_and_myths.claim: Polaris is the brightest star in the entire night sky.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Polaris ranks only as the 48th brightest star; Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Due to precession of Earth's axis, Polaris was not the North Star during Egyptian pyramid construction (Thuban was) and Vega will replace it in 12,000 years.

facts_and_myths.claim: Polaris is actually a triple star system rather than a single star.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It consists of the main supergiant Polaris Aa in close orbit with Polaris Ab, alongside a distant companion Polaris B.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Your latitude in the Northern Hemisphere directly equals the angle of Polaris above the horizon in degrees.

name: Sirius
visual_anchor: A dazzling diamond-blue star scintillating with blinding radiance against the cold winter midnight sky.
core_traits: Brightest star in Earth's entire night sky, shining at an apparent magnitude of -1.46
Located in the constellation Canis Major (The Greater Dog), earning it the title 'Dog Star'
Located relatively close to our solar system at just 8.6 light-years away
Binary star system orbited by a faint white dwarf companion known as 'The Pup' (Sirius B)

facts_and_myths.claim: The ancient Egyptians based their annual agricultural calendar on the morning rising of Sirius.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The heliacal rising of Sirius in mid-summer signaled the annual life-giving flooding of the Nile River.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The sweltering midsummer weeks are called the 'Dog Days of Summer' because Greeks believed Sirius added its heat to the Sun.

facts_and_myths.claim: Sirius is intrinsically the most luminous star in the entire universe.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sirius appears so bright primarily because it is very close to Earth (8.6 light-years); stars like Rigel are thousands of times more luminous.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sirius flashes rapidly in multiple rainbow colors near the horizon due to atmospheric turbulence.

name: Betelgeuse
visual_anchor: A titanic, pulsating deep ruby-orange supergiant star glowing menacingly at the right shoulder of Orion the Hunter.
core_traits: Luminous red supergiant star marking the upper-left shoulder of the constellation Orion
One of the largest stars visible to the naked eye, with a diameter over 700 times that of the Sun
Semiregular variable star located approximately 550 to 650 light-years from Earth
Expected to end its life in a spectacular core-collapse supernova within the next 100,000 years

facts_and_myths.claim: When Betelgeuse goes supernova, it will shine as bright as the full Moon for several months.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its supernova will be easily visible in broad daylight and cast shadows on Earth at night, while remaining at a completely safe distance.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In late 2019, Betelgeuse dimmed by over a full magnitude in the 'Great Dimming' when it ejected a massive surface dust cloud.

facts_and_myths.claim: Betelgeuse has already exploded and the shockwave will destroy Earth tomorrow.
facts_and_myths.explanation: At over 500 light-years away, any future supernova poses zero radiation danger to Earth's atmosphere or biosphere.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name Betelgeuse originates from the Arabic 'Ibt al-Jawza', meaning 'the armpit of the central one'.

name: Rigel
visual_anchor: A blinding ice-blue supergiant star blazing with crystalline intensity at the bottom left foot of Orion.
core_traits: Blazingly luminous blue supergiant star marking the left foot of the constellation Orion
Brightest star in Orion and the seventh-brightest star in Earth's entire night sky
Approximately 860 light-years from Earth, radiating with the luminosity of about 120,000 Suns
Multiple star system dominated by the primary blue-white supergiant Rigel A

facts_and_myths.claim: Rigel is actually intrinsically much brighter than Betelgeuse.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Rigel shines with over 100,000 solar luminosities, whereas Betelgeuse averages around 100,000, but Rigel's bluer light carries far higher energy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name Rigel comes from the Arabic 'Rijl Jauzah al Yusra', meaning 'the left leg of the central one'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Rigel is located closer to Earth than the planet Mars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Rigel is located roughly 860 light-years away in deep interstellar space, billions of times farther than Mars.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Rigel illuminates the nearby faint reflection nebula IC 2118, famously nicknamed the 'Witch Head Nebula'.

name: Alpha Centauri
visual_anchor: A brilliant golden-white binary star system glittering brightly beside the Southern Cross in the southern celestial hemisphere.
core_traits: Closest star system to our solar system, located approximately 4.37 light-years away
Triple star system consisting of Alpha Centauri A (Rigil Kentaurus), Alpha Centauri B (Toliman), and Proxima Centauri
Third-brightest star in the night sky as seen with the naked eye from Earth's Southern Hemisphere
Stars A and B are very similar to our Sun in mass, temperature, and composition

facts_and_myths.claim: Alpha Centauri is a single giant star like our Sun.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is a gravitationally bound triple star system composed of two Sun-like stars and a dim red dwarf (Proxima Centauri).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: To the naked eye, Alpha Centauri A and B blend together as one brilliant star.

facts_and_myths.claim: Alpha Centauri serves as one of the two 'Southern Pointers' used to locate the Southern Cross.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Alpha Centauri and neighboring Hadar (Beta Centauri) form a famous celestial pointer line pointing straight to Crux.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Breakthrough Starshot is a project proposing laser-propelled nanocraft to reach Alpha Centauri within 20 years of flight.

name: Proxima Centauri
visual_anchor: A faint crimson red dwarf star glowing dimly in the southern sky, orbited by rocky exoplanet Proxima b.
core_traits: Individual closest known star to the Sun, located approximately 4.2465 light-years away
Small, low-mass red dwarf star in the Alpha Centauri system with only about 12% of the Sun's mass
Invisible to the naked eye despite its proximity due to extremely low luminosity
Hosts Proxima Centauri b, an Earth-mass exoplanet orbiting within its habitable zone

facts_and_myths.claim: Although Proxima Centauri is the closest star to Earth, it is completely invisible without a telescope.
facts_and_myths.explanation: As a dim red dwarf with apparent magnitude 11.13, it shines at less than 1/1,000th the visual luminosity of our Sun.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Proxima Centauri is a flare star that frequently erupts with violent stellar flares that double its brightness in minutes.

facts_and_myths.claim: Human spacecraft have already visited Proxima Centauri and sent back surface photos.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Voyager 1, our fastest outgoing probe, would take over 73,000 years to reach the distance of Proxima Centauri.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Proxima b orbits its star in just 11.2 Earth days.

name: Vega
visual_anchor: A sapphire-white jewel star spinning at breakneck speed, surrounded by a faint glowing dust disk in Lyra.
core_traits: Fifth-brightest star in the night sky and second-brightest in the northern celestial hemisphere
Located just 25 light-years from Earth in the constellation Lyra
Serves as one vertex of the prominent northern Summer Triangle alongside Deneb and Altair
Historically served as the North Pole star around 12,000 BC and will do so again around 13,727 AD

facts_and_myths.claim: Vega was the first star other than the Sun ever to be photographed by astronomers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: William Cranch Bond and John Adams Whipple photographed Vega on a daguerreotype plate at Harvard Observatory on July 17, 1850.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Vega spins so rapidly (once every 12.5 hours) that centrifugal force causes its equator to bulge outward by 19%.

facts_and_myths.claim: Vega is a dying red supergiant on the verge of collapsing into a black hole.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Vega is a young, healthy blue-white main-sequence star only about 455 million years old.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Vega was the baseline reference star historically defined as magnitude 0.0 in photometric systems.

name: Aldebaran
visual_anchor: A piercing fiery orange giant star glowing angrily as the fiery eye of Taurus the Bull in front of the Hyades cluster.
core_traits: Brightest star in the zodiac constellation Taurus, shining with a distinct reddish-orange hue
Evolved red giant star about 44 times larger than our Sun, located roughly 65 light-years away
Appears visually at the center of the V-shaped Hyades star cluster, though it is physically twice as close to Earth
Name comes from the Arabic 'Al Dabaran', meaning 'The Follower', because it follows the Pleiades across the night sky

facts_and_myths.claim: NASA's Pioneer 10 spacecraft is currently drifting on a trajectory heading toward Aldebaran.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Pioneer 10 will make its closest approach to Aldebaran in approximately two million years.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Aldebaran has a confirmed giant exoplanet, Aldebaran b, which has roughly six times the mass of Jupiter.

facts_and_myths.claim: Aldebaran is physically bound inside the Hyades open star cluster.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Aldebaran is an accidental foreground star located 65 light-years away, while the Hyades cluster lies 150 light-years behind it.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Moon regularly passes directly in front of Aldebaran in dramatic lunar occultations.

name: Antares
visual_anchor: A blood-red pulsating supergiant star gleaming at the anatomical heart of the curving constellation Scorpius.
core_traits: Luminous red supergiant star marking the heart of the southern constellation Scorpius
Name translates from Greek as 'Rival to Ares (Mars)' due to its vivid reddish tint competing with the Red Planet
Colossal star with a radius roughly 680 times that of our Sun, located approximately 550 light-years away
Binary system accompanied by a faint blue-white companion star (Antares B)

facts_and_myths.claim: Antares was named 'Rival of Mars' because ancient stargazers often confused it with the red planet.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because both objects sit near the ecliptic and shine with a nearly identical fiery orange-red color, Greeks named it Anti-Ares.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: If Antares replaced our Sun, its outer atmosphere would engulf the orbits of Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars.

facts_and_myths.claim: Antares is a solid ball of iron located inside our Oort cloud.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Antares is a thermonuclear gas supergiant located hundreds of light-years away in interstellar space.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Antares is surrounded by the colorful Rho Ophiuchi cloud complex, one of the most photographed nebulae in the sky.

name: Arcturus
visual_anchor: A radiant golden-orange giant star blazing near the tail of the Great Bear in the northern spring sky.
core_traits: Brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere and fourth-brightest star in the night sky overall
Orange giant star located roughly 36.7 light-years from Earth in the constellation Bootes
Easily located by following the arc of the Big Dipper's handle ('Follow the arc to Arcturus')
High proper motion star barreling through our galactic neighborhood at over 120 kilometers per second

facts_and_myths.claim: Starlight from Arcturus was used to turn on the lights for the 1933 Chicago World's Fair.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Photoelectric cells focused light from Arcturus to celebrate 40 years since the 1893 fair, matching its estimated 40-light-year distance.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Arcturus is part of the 'Arcturus Stream', a group of stars likely left behind by an ancient dwarf galaxy consumed by the Milky Way.

facts_and_myths.claim: Arcturus is a member of the Zodiac constellations.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Arcturus is located in the northern constellation Bootes (the Herdsman), well outside the zodiac path.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its name in ancient Greek means 'Guardian of the Bear' due to its position trailing Ursa Major.

name: Canopus
visual_anchor: A brilliant pearl-white supergiant star commanding the southern skies second only to Sirius in nocturnal brightness.
core_traits: Second-brightest star in Earth's entire night sky with an apparent visual magnitude of -0.74
Brightest star in the southern constellation Carina (The Keel of Argo Navis)
Luminous bright giant of spectral type A9 located approximately 310 light-years from Earth
Extensively used by spacecraft attitude control systems as a bright optical navigational guide star

facts_and_myths.claim: Robotic spacecraft like Mariner and Voyager used Canopus to navigate through the solar system.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Canopus's high brightness and location far from the ecliptic plane made it the perfect target for star trackers to orient spacecraft in 3D space.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Because it lies deep in the southern sky, Canopus cannot be seen from Europe or the northern United States.

facts_and_myths.claim: Canopus is dimmer than planet Saturn at all times.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Canopus is so exceptionally luminous (10,000 times brighter than our Sun) that only Sirius outshines it among stars in the night sky.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Canopus is named after the legendary ship navigator for King Menelaus of Sparta in Homer's Iliad.

name: Spica
visual_anchor: A sparkling blue-white binary star shining proudly in the constellation Virgo, located by speeding on from Arcturus.
core_traits: Brightest star in the constellation Virgo and the 16th-brightest star in the night sky
Spectroscopic binary star system located approximately 250 light-years away from Earth
Easily located via the mnemonic 'Follow the arc to Arcturus, and speed on to Spica'
Name comes from the Latin 'Spica virginis', meaning 'Virgo's ear of grain/wheat'

facts_and_myths.claim: Hipparchus discovered the precession of the equinoxes by measuring the motion of Spica in 127 BC.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Comparing Spica's position with records from Timocharis 150 years earlier, Hipparchus proved Earth's rotational axis wobbles.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The two stars of Spica orbit each other every 4 days, so close that mutual gravity distorts them into egg shapes.

facts_and_myths.claim: Spica is a lone red dwarf star.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Spica consists of two massive, hot blue giant stars that burn at temperatures over 20,000 Kelvin.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Spica is depicted on the national flag of Brazil, representing the federal state of Para.

name: Pollux
visual_anchor: A warm golden-orange giant star shining brightly beside its twin Castor at the heads of the Gemini constellation.
core_traits: Brightest star in the constellation Gemini, outshining its mythological twin Castor
Orange giant star located roughly 34 light-years from Earth
Has an extrasolar planet, Thestias (Pollux b), confirmed in orbit around it in 2006
Named after Polydeuces, the immortal twin son of Zeus and Leda in Greek mythology

facts_and_myths.claim: Although designated Beta Geminorum, Pollux is actually brighter than Alpha Geminorum (Castor).
facts_and_myths.explanation: Johann Bayer designated Castor as Alpha and Pollux as Beta in 1603 based on northern position, even though Pollux shines brighter.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pollux is the closest giant star to our Sun.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pollux and Castor are physically orbiting each other as a binary pair.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They appear close together in the sky by perspective; Pollux is 34 light-years away, while Castor is 51 light-years away.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pollux's planet Thestias is a gas giant with at least twice the mass of Jupiter.

name: Castor
visual_anchor: A pure white star system at the head of Gemini, which telescopes reveal to be a sextuple system of six gravitationally bound stars.
core_traits: Second-brightest star in the constellation Gemini, partnering with Pollux
Fascinating sextuple star system consisting of three pairs of binary stars orbiting a common center of gravity
Located approximately 51 light-years from Earth
Radiant point of the prolific Geminid meteor shower in mid-December

facts_and_myths.claim: Castor is not just one star, but six distinct stars bound together by gravity.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Telescopic and spectroscopic analysis reveals Castor is a sextuple system composed of three pairs of binary stars.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Greek mythology, Castor was the mortal twin, renowned as a master tamer of horses.

facts_and_myths.claim: Castor was destroyed in a supernova explosion witnessed in 1999.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Castor is completely intact and stable, continuing to shine brightly in Gemini.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Geminid meteor shower appears to radiate directly from the vicinity of Castor.

name: Deneb
visual_anchor: A majestic white supergiant crowning the northern cross of Cygnus the Swan at the apex of the Summer Triangle.
core_traits: Brightest star in the constellation Cygnus (The Swan) and 19th-brightest star in the night sky
Colossal white supergiant star located roughly 2,600 light-years away from Earth
One of the most intrinsically luminous stars visible to the naked eye (roughly 200,000 times brighter than the Sun)
Forms the Summer Triangle asterism along with Vega and Altair

facts_and_myths.claim: Deneb is so intrinsically luminous that if it were as close to Earth as Sirius, it would shine as bright as the full Moon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Shining from a staggering 2,600 light-years away, Deneb is among the most distant first-magnitude stars visible without a telescope.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name Deneb comes from the Arabic 'Dhanab ad-Dajajah', meaning 'tail of the hen (swan)'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Deneb will never run out of nuclear fuel.
facts_and_myths.explanation: As a massive supergiant, Deneb burns fuel rapidly and will likely detonate in a supernova within a few million years.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Deneb serves as the prototype for a class of pulsating variable stars known as Alpha Cygni variables.

name: Altair
visual_anchor: A fast-spinning oblate white star flattened at its poles, completing the southern vertex of the Summer Triangle in Aquila.
core_traits: Brightest star in the constellation Aquila (The Eagle) and twelfth-brightest star in the night sky
White main-sequence star located relatively close to Earth at roughly 16.7 light-years
Rotates at extreme speed (roughly 286 km/s at the equator), flattening it into an oblate spheroid
Third corner of the prominent northern Summer Triangle asterism with Vega and Deneb

facts_and_myths.claim: Altair spins so fast that its equator completes a rotation in roughly 9 hours, causing it to bulge outward like a squashed ball.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Centrifugal force flattens Altair's equatorial radius to 20% wider than its polar radius, verified by optical interferometry in 2007.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its rapid rotation causes gravity darkening, making its equator cooler and dimmer than its poles.

facts_and_myths.claim: Altair is the mythological name for an ancient Egyptian crocodile.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Altair comes from the Arabic phrase 'an-nasr at-ta'ir', meaning 'the flying eagle'.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the East Asian Qixi/Tanabata legend, Altair represents the Cowherd separated from the Weaver Girl (Vega) by the Milky Way.

name: Bellatrix
visual_anchor: A hot blue-white giant star gleaming aggressively at the left shoulder of Orion the Hunter opposite Betelgeuse.
core_traits: Third-brightest star in the constellation Orion, marking Orion's right (west) shoulder
Hot blue-white giant star of spectral type B2 located roughly 250 light-years away
Name is Latin for 'female warrior' or 'Amazon star'
Used as a historical standard star for luminosity calibration before being discovered to be slightly variable

facts_and_myths.claim: Bellatrix was named after a famous character in the Harry Potter book series.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Author J.K. Rowling named the character Bellatrix Lestrange after the ancient Roman star name, which has existed for thousands of years.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bellatrix has a surface temperature around 22,000 Kelvin, nearly four times hotter than our Sun.

facts_and_myths.claim: Bellatrix is about six times more massive than our Sun.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With a mass around 8.6 solar masses, it is on the borderline of stars that could collapse into a white dwarf or go supernova.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Unlike Betelgeuse which is expanding as a red supergiant, Bellatrix is still a blue giant fusing hydrogen.

name: VY Canis Majoris
visual_anchor: A gargantuan crimson red hypergiant star churning amid a massive expanding cloud of ejected gas and silicate dust.
core_traits: Extreme oxygen-rich red hypergiant star in the constellation Canis Major
One of the largest known stars by radius, measuring roughly 1,420 times the radius of the Sun
Located approximately 3,900 light-years away from Earth
Surrounded by a complex circumstellar envelope created by violent mass-loss eruptions

facts_and_myths.claim: If an airplane flew along the equator of VY Canis Majoris at 900 km/h, it would take over 1,100 years to complete one lap.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With a circumference of over 9 billion kilometers, its immense size boggles human comprehension.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Light, which circles Earth in 0.13 seconds, takes over 8 hours just to travel around VY Canis Majoris.

facts_and_myths.claim: VY Canis Majoris is denser than lead throughout its entire body.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because its mass is spread over an unfathomable volume, its outer atmosphere is extremely rarefied, a billion times less dense than air on Earth.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It is shedding mass at a rate of 30 Earth masses every single year.

name: UY Scuti
