visual_anchor: A colossal red supergiant pulsating weakly in the southern constellation Scutum, vast enough to swallow Jupiter's orbit.
core_traits: Extreme red supergiant star located approximately 9,500 light-years away in the constellation Scutum
Ranked among the largest known stars by radius, historically estimated at up to 1,700 solar radii
Pulsates semiregularly over a cycle of roughly 740 days
So vast that its volume could hold approximately 5 billion Suns

facts_and_myths.claim: UY Scuti could comfortably contain about 5 billion spheres the size of our Sun inside its volume.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because volume scales with the cube of the radius, a radius of 1,700 solar radii yields over 4.9 billion solar volumes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: If placed at the center of our solar system, its surface would extend well past the orbit of Jupiter.

facts_and_myths.claim: UY Scuti is the heaviest star in the universe by weight.
facts_and_myths.explanation: UY Scuti is huge in physical size, but its mass is only about 7 to 10 solar masses; stars like R136a1 are vastly heavier (over 200 solar masses).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Gaia satellite parallax measurements recently revised its distance and radius estimates slightly downward.

name: Stephenson 2-18
visual_anchor: A mind-boggling red hypergiant star of unimaginable scale, dwarfing all nearby stars in the open cluster Stephenson 2.
core_traits: Red hypergiant star in the constellation Scutum, member of the open cluster Stephenson 2
Currently recognized as one of the largest stars known in the universe, with an estimated radius of 2,150 solar radii
Located approximately 19,000 light-years from Earth
Could hold roughly 10 billion Suns inside its physical boundary

facts_and_myths.claim: If placed at the center of our solar system, the surface of Stephenson 2-18 would engulf the orbit of Saturn.
facts_and_myths.explanation: At 2,150 solar radii (nearly 10 astronomical units), its photosphere would extend to roughly 1.5 billion kilometers from the center.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A ray of light traveling at 300,000 km/s would take nearly 9 hours to complete a single trip around its equator.

facts_and_myths.claim: Stephenson 2-18 was discovered by Galileo Galilei in 1609.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It was discovered in 1990 by American astronomer Charles Bruce Stephenson using deep-sky infrared survey data.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its luminosity is estimated at roughly 440,000 times that of the Sun.

name: Orion
visual_anchor: A magnificent celestial warrior outlined by bright stars, wielding a club and shield with a distinct belt of three aligned stars.
core_traits: One of the most recognizable and famous constellations in the night sky, visible worldwide from both hemispheres
Represents the mythical Greek hunter Orion battling Taurus the Bull
Anchored by supergiant stars Betelgeuse (shoulder) and Rigel (foot)
Features Orion's Belt, a distinctive asterism of three bright aligned stars (Alnitak, Alnilam, Mintaka)

facts_and_myths.claim: The constellation Orion can be seen from everywhere on Earth except the extreme poles.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because Orion sits directly on the celestial equator, it is visible from almost every inhabited continent on the globe.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The three pyramids of Giza in Egypt are famously claimed by some theorists to align with the three stars of Orion's Belt.

facts_and_myths.claim: All the stars in Orion are connected to each other by cosmic laser strings.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The stars appear in a 2D pattern from Earth's line of sight, but are separated by hundreds of light-years in true 3D space.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Greek mythology, Orion was placed in the sky opposite Scorpius so the hunter and the scorpion could never meet.

name: Ursa Major
visual_anchor: A massive northern constellation resembling a prowling bear, enclosing the brilliant spoon shape of the Big Dipper.
core_traits: Third-largest constellation in the sky, prominent in the northern hemisphere year-round
Contains the famous seven-star asterism known as the Big Dipper or the Plough
Two stars on the outer bowl (Merak and Dubhe) serve as 'The Pointers' to find Polaris
Identified as a bear across completely independent ancient cultures in Greece, Siberia, and Native North America

facts_and_myths.claim: Ancient Native Americans and ancient Greeks both independently named this constellation a 'Bear' without contact.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Anthropologists trace the 'Cosmic Hunt' bear myth back over 15,000 years to Paleolithic hunter-gatherers crossing the Bering land bridge.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mizar and Alcor in the bear's tail were used by ancient Arab warriors as an eye test for archery recruitment.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ursa Major is identical to the Big Dipper.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Big Dipper is merely a small seven-star asterism forming the bear's rear torso and tail; the full constellation Ursa Major is vastly larger.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ursa Major contains the famous interacting galaxies M81 and M82.

name: Ursa Minor
visual_anchor: A delicate northern constellation curving upward from the brilliant anchor star Polaris at the tip of its tail.
core_traits: Northern constellation famous for hosting the north celestial pole and Polaris (the North Star)
Contains the seven-star asterism known as the Little Dipper
Polaris marks the tip of the Little Bear's tail
Circumpolar constellation that never sets below the horizon for observers in mid-to-high northern latitudes

facts_and_myths.claim: The tail of the Little Bear is anchored by the most important navigational star in human history.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Polaris, located at the end of Ursa Minor's tail, points almost exactly to the true north celestial pole.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Greek mythology, Ursa Minor represents Arcas, the son of Callisto (Ursa Major), both turned into bears and hurled into the heavens by Zeus.

facts_and_myths.claim: All seven stars of the Little Dipper are as bright as the North Star.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Aside from Polaris and the outer bowl stars Kochab and Pherkad, the four middle stars are quite faint and easily washed out by city light pollution.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It was officially cataloged by Greek astronomer Ptolemy in the 2nd century.

name: Big Dipper
visual_anchor: Seven bright stars tracing the unmistakable outline of a giant water ladle or frying pan across the northern night sky.
core_traits: World-famous seven-star asterism located within the constellation Ursa Major
Composed of stars Alkaid, Mizar, Alioth, Megrez, Phecda, Merak, and Dubhe
The outer two bowl stars (Merak and Dubhe) point in a straight line directly to Polaris
Known as the Plough in the UK and Ireland, and the Celestial Ladle in East Asia

facts_and_myths.claim: The Big Dipper is an officially recognized 88 modern constellation.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is an asterism (a popular recognizable pattern of stars), not an official constellation; it is part of the larger constellation Ursa Major.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Enslaved people in the American South used the 'Drinking Gourd' (Big Dipper) as a secret navigational guide leading north to freedom on the Underground Railroad.

facts_and_myths.claim: Five of the seven stars in the Big Dipper belong to a single traveling star cluster moving together through space.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Ursa Major Moving Group is a family of stars born together about 300 million years ago, sharing identical speed and trajectory through the galaxy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Over the next 100,000 years, proper motion will warp the ladle shape into an unrecognizable zigzag.

name: Cassiopeia
visual_anchor: Five bright stars forming a prominent zig-zag letter 'W' (or 'M') gleaming opposite the Big Dipper across the North Star.
core_traits: Northern circumpolar constellation easily recognized by its distinct 'W' or 'M' shape formed by five bright stars
Located in the Milky Way opposite the Big Dipper across the north celestial pole
Named after Queen Cassiopeia of Greek mythology, who was punished for her boastful vanity
Home to Tycho's Supernova remnant (SN 1572) and the powerful radio source Cassiopeia A

facts_and_myths.claim: In Greek myth, Cassiopeia was chained to her celestial throne upside down for half the year as punishment for vanity.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Poseidon punished her for boasting she and her daughter Andromeda were more beautiful than the sea nymphs (Nereids).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Tycho Brahe observed his famous 1572 supernova in Cassiopeia, proving the heavens beyond the Moon were not unchanging.

facts_and_myths.claim: Cassiopeia is only visible from the South Pole.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cassiopeia is a northern constellation and is never visible from southern latitudes below 20 degrees south.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Cassiopeia A is the strongest discrete astronomical radio source in the sky outside the solar system.

name: Southern Cross
visual_anchor: Four brilliant diamond stars forming a distinct kite or cross pattern glowing beside the dark silhouette of the Coalsack Nebula.
core_traits: Smallest of all 88 modern constellations, located in the southern celestial hemisphere
Forms a distinctive cross or kite pattern that points directly toward the South Celestial Pole
Featured on the national flags of Australia, New Zealand, Brazil, Papua New Guinea, and Samoa
Composed of four main bright stars: Acrux, Mimosa, Gacrux, and Imai

facts_and_myths.claim: The Southern Cross is depicted on more national flags than any other constellation.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Australia, New Zealand, Brazil, Papua New Guinea, and Samoa all proudly display Crux on their national banners.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The top star Gacrux is a red giant, while the other three stars are hot blue-white B-type stars.

facts_and_myths.claim: There is a bright South Star sitting right at the southern celestial pole like Polaris in the north.
facts_and_myths.explanation: There is no bright southern pole star; southern navigators must use the long axis of the Southern Cross extended 4.5 times to find south.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Directly adjacent to the cross lies the Coalsack Nebula, a prominent dark absorption nebula.

name: Canis Major
visual_anchor: A canine-shaped constellation bounding behind Orion, anchored by the blinding radiance of Sirius at its canine chest.
core_traits: Prominent southern constellation representing the larger of Orion's two hunting dogs
Home to Sirius, the brightest star in Earth's entire night sky
Located in the winter sky just southeast of the constellation Orion
Contains the bright open star cluster M41 and the red hypergiant VY Canis Majoris

facts_and_myths.claim: In Greek mythology, Canis Major represents Laelaps, a magical dog destined to always catch whatever it chased.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Zeus placed Laelaps in the sky after it engaged in an endless paradox chasing the Teumessian fox, which could never be caught.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Canis Major contains the dwarf galaxy Canis Major Dwarf, thought to be the closest neighboring galaxy to our solar system.

facts_and_myths.claim: Canis Major is a northern constellation visible only from the Arctic.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is a southern celestial constellation, best seen in the winter evening sky from both hemispheres.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ancient Romans sacrificed a red dog in spring to appease Sirius and protect their crops.

name: Cygnus
visual_anchor: A graceful celestial swan with wide outstretched wings soaring down the luminous glowing river of the Milky Way.
core_traits: Prominent northern constellation shaped like a flying swan or a cross (the Northern Cross)
Anchored by first-magnitude supergiant star Deneb at the swan's tail
Features Albireo at the swan's beak, one of the most famous gold-and-sapphire double stars in the sky
Hosts Cygnus X-1, the first widely accepted stellar-mass black hole candidate discovered in astronomy

facts_and_myths.claim: The star at the beak of Cygnus, Albireo, is universally considered the most beautiful colored double star in amateur astronomy.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Through even a small telescope, Albireo splits into a contrasting golden-topaz giant and a sparkling sapphire-blue companion.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Cygnus sits right in the thickest, richest stellar stream of the northern Milky Way.

facts_and_myths.claim: Cygnus is located on the surface of planet Mars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cygnus is an astronomical star pattern spanning thousands of light-years in the Milky Way.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Greek myth, Cygnus represents Zeus disguised as a swan to seduce Leda.

name: Scorpius
visual_anchor: A curving hook of brilliant stars tracing a giant scorpion with raised claws and a stinging tail curling above the southern horizon.
core_traits: Distinctive zodiac constellation whose curved stars truly resemble its namesake scorpion
Anchored by the glowing red supergiant Antares ('Heart of the Scorpion')
Features a curling tail ending in the prominent stinger star Shaula
Located close to the galactic center of the Milky Way, rich in star clusters like the Butterfly and Ptolemy clusters

facts_and_myths.claim: In Polynesian mythology, the curving tail of Scorpius is the magic fishhook of demigod Maui.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Maui used the hook (known as Manaiakalani) to pull up the North Island of New Zealand from the bottom of the ocean.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Scorpius and Orion are on opposite sides of the sky, honoring the myth where the scorpion stung Orion to death.

facts_and_myths.claim: Scorpius is only visible during daytime with special radar goggles.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Scorpius is one of the most prominent, unmistakable naked-eye constellations visible on warm summer nights.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Sun spends only 7 days passing through Scorpius before entering Ophiuchus.

name: Taurus
visual_anchor: A charging celestial bull with long gleaming horns, anchored by the fiery orange eye of Aldebaran and the sparkling Pleiades cluster.
core_traits: Prominent northern winter zodiac constellation representing a charging bull
Dominated by the bright red giant star Aldebaran marking the bull's fiery eye
Hosts two of the closest and most famous open star clusters: the Pleiades and the Hyades
Features the Crab Nebula (M1), remnant of the famous 1054 AD supernova

facts_and_myths.claim: Cave paintings in Lascaux, France, dating back 17,000 years depict the constellation Taurus and the Pleiades.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Astronomers and archaeologists agree that the 'Hall of the Bulls' paintings align accurately with the stars of Taurus and the Seven Sisters.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Greek mythology, Zeus transformed into a magnificent white bull (Taurus) to abduct princess Europa.

facts_and_myths.claim: Taurus is made entirely of dark matter with no visible stars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Taurus contains dozens of bright naked-eye stars and two of the brightest star clusters in the heavens.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The V-shaped head of the bull is formed by the Hyades star cluster.

name: Leo
visual_anchor: A majestic celestial lion outlined by a backward question mark (the Sickle) and the blue-white diamond star Regulus.
core_traits: Famous northern spring zodiac constellation representing the Nemean Lion slain by Hercules
Easily recognized by 'The Sickle', a backward question mark asterism outlining the lion's head and mane
Anchored by first-magnitude star Regulus ('The Little King') at the lion's chest
Radiant point for the famous annual Leonid meteor shower in November

facts_and_myths.claim: The Leonid meteor shower from Leo produced the most spectacular meteor storm in recorded human history in 1833.
facts_and_myths.explanation: On November 12, 1833, over 100,000 meteors fell per hour, lighting up North American skies and giving birth to modern meteor astronomy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Leo contains the famous 'Leo Triplet', a group of three interacting spiral galaxies (M65, M66, and NGC 3628).

facts_and_myths.claim: The constellation Leo was invented in 1969 to celebrate the Moon landing.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Leo is one of the oldest recognized constellations, documented by Mesopotamians and ancient Egyptians over 4,000 years ago.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Denebola, marking the lion's tail, comes from the Arabic 'Dhanab al-Asad' (tail of the lion).

name: Pegasus
visual_anchor: A giant square of four bright stars galloping upside down across the northern autumn sky, outlining the body of the winged horse.
core_traits: Prominent northern autumn constellation representing the mythical winged horse Pegasus
Dominated by the 'Great Square of Pegasus', a large rectangular asterism of four stars
Hosts 51 Pegasi, the first Sun-like star discovered to harbor an exoplanet (51 Pegasi b) in 1995
Contains Stephan's Quintet, a famous compact visual group of five interacting galaxies

facts_and_myths.claim: The 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for discovering the first exoplanet around a star in Pegasus.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz detected 51 Pegasi b in 1995, launching the modern era of exoplanet science.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In classical mythology, Pegasus sprang from the severed neck of Medusa when Perseus defeated her.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Great Square of Pegasus contains thousands of naked-eye stars inside its borders.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Under typical suburban skies, the inside of the Great Square looks almost completely black and empty, containing only a handful of faint stars.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: One of the four stars of the Great Square, Alpheratz, is officially shared with the neighboring constellation Andromeda.

name: Andromeda Constellation
visual_anchor: A horn-shaped chain of stars branching outward from the Great Square of Pegasus, cradling the spiral smudge of the Andromeda Galaxy.
core_traits: Northern constellation named after the mythical princess Andromeda, chained to a rock as a sacrifice to Cetus
Located north of the celestial equator, adjacent to Perseus, Pegasus, and Cassiopeia
World-famous for containing the Andromeda Galaxy (M31), the nearest major spiral galaxy to our own
Anchored by bright stars Alpheratz, Mirach, and Almach

facts_and_myths.claim: You can find the Andromeda Galaxy by star-hopping from the star Mirach in the Andromeda constellation.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Stargazers hop from Mirach through Mu Andromedae straight to Nu Andromedae to spot the glowing disk of M31.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Almach at the foot of Andromeda is a breathtaking quadruple star system with striking golden-orange and emerald-cyan colors.

facts_and_myths.claim: The constellation Andromeda is an actual galaxy that is colliding with the Sun today.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The constellation is a geometric pattern of Milky Way stars; the Andromeda Galaxy is a separate object millions of light-years behind them.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Persian astronomer Abd al-Rahman al-Sufi documented the Andromeda Galaxy in this constellation in 964 AD as a 'little cloud'.

name: Centaurus
visual_anchor: A sprawling, brilliant southern constellation representing a mythical half-man half-horse surrounding the Southern Cross.
core_traits: One of the largest constellations in the sky, prominent in the southern celestial hemisphere
Contains the Alpha Centauri star system, our closest stellar neighbors
Home to Omega Centauri, the largest and brightest globular cluster in the entire Milky Way
Features Centaurus A (NGC 5128), one of the closest and most powerful radio galaxies to Earth

facts_and_myths.claim: Omega Centauri inside this constellation contains approximately 10 million stars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is so massive and dense that astronomers suspect it is the stripped core of an ancient dwarf galaxy consumed by the Milky Way.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Omega Centauri is easily visible to the naked eye as a fuzzy star of magnitude 3.7.

facts_and_myths.claim: Centaurus is the exact same constellation as Sagittarius.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They are two distinct constellations representing different centaurs: Centaurus represents wise Chiron, while Sagittarius represents an archer.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its two brightest stars, Alpha and Beta Centauri, are known as the Southern Pointers pointing directly to Crux.

name: Pleiades
visual_anchor: A shimmering cluster of brilliant sapphire-blue young stars veiled in a delicate, gossamer reflection nebula in Taurus.
core_traits: Open star cluster located in the constellation Taurus, approximately 444 light-years from Earth
One of the nearest and most obvious star clusters to the naked eye, known across every ancient human culture
Dominated by hot, luminous blue B-type stars born within the last 100 million years
Features prominent stars named after the seven mythological sisters: Alcyone, Maia, Electra, Taygeta, Celaeno, Merope, and Asterope

facts_and_myths.claim: The Japanese automotive company Subaru took its name and logo directly from the Pleiades star cluster.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Subaru is the Japanese name for the Pleiades, and the car company's logo depicts the cluster's six brightest stars.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Most people with good eyesight see six stars with the naked eye; under dark skies, up to 14 stars can be resolved.

facts_and_myths.claim: The blue reflection haze surrounding the Pleiades is leftover gas from which the stars were originally born.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Spectroscopy shows the stars are merely passing by chance through an unrelated cloud of interstellar dust at high speed.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Greek mythology, Orion pursued the Seven Sisters across the sky until Zeus turned them into doves and set them among the stars.

name: Hyades
visual_anchor: A wide V-shaped wedge of golden and orange stars forming the face of Taurus the Bull in the winter night sky.
core_traits: Nearest open star cluster to our solar system, located approximately 153 light-years away
Forms a distinctive V-shaped asterism representing the head and face of Taurus the Bull
Contains roughly 300 to 400 stars sharing a common origin, age, and motion through space
Aldebaran appears visually in the V-shape but is an unrelated foreground star twice as close

facts_and_myths.claim: The bright orange star Aldebaran is the mother star of the Hyades cluster.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Aldebaran is an accidental foreground star 65 light-years away, completely unrelated to the Hyades cluster 153 light-years behind it.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Hyades has an estimated age of 625 million years, roughly six times older than the neighboring Pleiades.

facts_and_myths.claim: In ancient Greece, the rising of the Hyades in autumn was believed to bring rain.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their name comes from the Greek 'hyein', meaning 'to rain', because their heliacal rising coincided with the rainy season.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Hyades cluster is slowly dispersing over time due to gravitational tidal disruption from the Milky Way.

name: Zodiac
visual_anchor: An illuminated celestial ring wrapping around the night sky along the ecliptic path of the Sun, Moon, and major planets.
core_traits: Belt-shaped region of the celestial sphere that extends roughly 8 degrees north or south of the ecliptic
Path through which the Sun, Moon, and major planets appear to travel across the sky throughout the year
Divided historically into 12 signs of 30 degrees each, named after constellations along the path
Originates from the Greek word 'zodiakos kyklos', meaning 'circle of little animals'

facts_and_myths.claim: Astronomically, the Sun actually passes through 13 constellations along the ecliptic, not 12.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Sun spends about two to three weeks traveling through the constellation Ophiuchus (the Serpent Bearer) between Scorpius and Sagittarius.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Because of axial precession, the dates when the Sun is in astronomical constellations have shifted by almost a whole month since Babylonian times.

facts_and_myths.claim: Scientific tests have proved your zodiac sign dictates your career, marriage success, and personality.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Extensive scientific and statistical studies have consistently demonstrated zero correlation between astronomical zodiac signs and human lives.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Babylonian astronomers created the 12-sign zodiac around the 5th century BC to match their 12-month calendar.

name: Sagittarius Constellation
visual_anchor: A celestial archer aiming an arrow toward Scorpius, containing a famous asterism that looks exactly like a steaming teapot.
core_traits: Southern zodiac constellation representing a centaur aiming a bow and arrow
Famous for containing the 'Teapot' asterism, complete with handle, lid, spout, and steam
Points directly toward the true galactic center of the Milky Way and supermassive black hole Sagittarius A*
Packed with spectacular deep-sky targets including the Lagoon Nebula, Trifid Nebula, and Omega Nebula

facts_and_myths.claim: Looking toward Sagittarius means you are looking straight at the heart and center of our entire galaxy.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The rotational center of the Milky Way, including Sagittarius A*, lies directly behind the stars of this constellation.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The starry 'steam' rising from the Teapot's spout is actually the dense central star cloud of the Milky Way.

facts_and_myths.claim: The famous Wow! Signal detected by SETI in 1977 originated in the direction of Sagittarius.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The mysterious 72-second narrowband radio signal detected by the Big Ear telescope came from the constellation Sagittarius.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sagittarius contains 15 Messier objects, more than any other constellation in the sky.

name: Gemini Constellation
visual_anchor: Two parallel stick-figure twins standing side-by-side in the northern winter sky, crowned by bright stars Castor and Pollux.
core_traits: Prominent zodiac constellation in the northern winter sky representing the twin brothers Castor and Pollux
Easily spotted northeast of Orion by its two bright namesake stars at the heads of the twins
Radiant origin point for the prolific Geminid meteor shower every December
Discovered to host planet Uranus by William Herschel in 1781 while observing near Propus

facts_and_myths.claim: Clyde Tombaugh discovered the dwarf planet Pluto in 1930 while photographing the constellation Gemini.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tombaugh spotted Pluto moving against the background stars of Gemini using the blink comparator at Lowell Observatory.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: NASA named the two-man Project Gemini spaceflight program in the 1960s after the Twin constellation.

facts_and_myths.claim: Gemini is only visible from the South Pole during July.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Gemini is a northern constellation, prominent overhead during northern winter months.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Greek myth, Castor and Pollux were Argonauts who sailed with Jason to retrieve the Golden Fleece.

name: Aries
visual_anchor: A compact bent line of three stars in the northern autumn sky representing the golden-fleeced flying ram of Greek myth.
core_traits: First sign of the traditional zodiac, historically marking the vernal equinox (the 'First Point of Aries')
Mid-sized northern constellation representing the golden-fleeced ram that rescued Phrixus and Helle
Anchored by second-magnitude star Hamal (Alpha Arietis)
Located between Pisces to the west and Taurus to the east

facts_and_myths.claim: The vernal equinox is still located in the constellation Aries today.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Due to axial precession over 2,000 years, the equinox has drifted westward out of Aries and currently resides in Pisces.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The fleece of this mythological ram became the famous Golden Fleece sought by Jason and the Argonauts.

facts_and_myths.claim: Alpha Arietis, or Hamal, is an orange giant star with a confirmed orbiting exoplanet.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In 2011, astronomers discovered an exoplanet with roughly 1.8 times the mass of Jupiter orbiting Hamal.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name Hamal comes from the Arabic 'Ras al-Hamal', meaning 'head of the ram'.

name: Aquarius
visual_anchor: A faint southern zodiac constellation depicting a figure pouring a stream of water from an urn into the mouth of the Southern Fish.
core_traits: Large but relatively faint zodiac constellation located in a region of the sky called 'The Sea' or 'The Water'
Represents a man pouring an unending stream of water from an urn
Hosts the famous Helix Nebula ('Eye of God') and the Saturn Nebula
Radiant for the Eta Aquariid meteor shower produced by debris from Halley's Comet

facts_and_myths.claim: The TRAPPIST-1 star system, famous for hosting seven Earth-sized rocky planets, is located in Aquarius.
facts_and_myths.explanation: TRAPPIST-1 is an ultra-cool red dwarf star located 40 light-years away in the constellation Aquarius.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Three of TRAPPIST-1's planets are in the habitable Goldilocks zone where liquid water could exist.

facts_and_myths.claim: The musical song 'Age of Aquarius' refers to a scientifically verified astrological law of nature.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The 'Age of Aquarius' is a cultural and counterculture astrological concept, not a defined physical law.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Greek mythology, Aquarius was identified with Ganymede, the handsome Trojan youth who became cupbearer to the gods.

name: Pisces
visual_anchor: A large, faint V-shaped constellation depicting two fish swimming in perpendicular directions tied together by a ribbon.
core_traits: Zodiac constellation located between Aquarius to the west and Aries to the east
Depicts two fish swimming in different directions, tied at their tails by an ornamental ribbon
Currently hosts the 'First Point of Aries' (the Northern Hemisphere's vernal equinox location)
Contains the magnificent grand-design spiral galaxy M74 (the Phantom Galaxy)

facts_and_myths.claim: The astronomical vernal equinox currently lies within the constellation Pisces.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because Earth wobbles like a spinning top, the March equinox sun sits against the stars of Pisces, where it will remain until around 2600 AD.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Greek myth, Aphrodite and Eros transformed into fish and tied themselves together with a rope to escape the monster Typhon.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pisces contains the brightest star in the entire sky.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Pisces has no first-magnitude stars; its brightest star, Eta Piscium, is relatively faint at magnitude 3.6.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The James Webb Space Telescope took an astonishing infrared image of spiral galaxy M74 in Pisces in 2022.

name: Virgo
visual_anchor: The second-largest constellation in the sky, crowned by brilliant blue-white Spica and housing thousands of distant galaxies.
core_traits: Second-largest constellation in the entire night sky after Hydra, and largest in the Zodiac
Anchored by first-magnitude star Spica, held like an ear of wheat in the maiden's hand
Contains the Virgo Cluster, the heart of our local supercluster containing over 1,300 galaxies
Home to supermassive black hole host galaxy Messier 87

facts_and_myths.claim: The supermassive black hole at the center of galaxy M87, located in Virgo, was the first black hole ever directly photographed.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Event Horizon Telescope published the historic orange donut-ring photo of M87* in April 2019.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Virgo represents Astraea, the virgin goddess of justice in Greek mythology, holding the scales of justice (neighboring Libra).

facts_and_myths.claim: Virgo is composed of only three stars in the entire sky.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Virgo covers an enormous area of 1,294 square degrees and contains thousands of telescopic galaxies.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Sombrero Galaxy (M104) is located on the southern border of Virgo.

name: Libra
visual_anchor: A symmetrical diamond-shaped constellation representing the balancing pans of the scales of justice between Virgo and Scorpius.
core_traits: Zodiac constellation situated between Virgo to the west and Scorpius to the east
Only zodiac constellation that represents an inanimate object (the weighing scales) rather than an animal or mythological figure
Main stars Zubeneschamali and Zubenelgenubi were historically regarded as the claws of the scorpion
Home to Methuselah star (HD 140283), one of the oldest known stars in the universe

facts_and_myths.claim: Libra is the only sign of the zodiac that does not symbolize a living creature.
facts_and_myths.explanation: All 11 other zodiac constellations depict animals, humans, or mythical human-animal hybrids; Libra alone represents a balance scale.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Star Zubeneschamali (Beta Librae) is described by many stargazers as the only naked-eye star appearing distinctly green.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Methuselah star in Libra is proven to be 50 billion years old, older than the universe.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Early calculations yielded an age of 14.5 billion years with a +/-0.8 billion margin of error, perfectly consistent with the 13.8-billion-year age of the cosmos.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The names Zubenelgenubi and Zubeneschamali mean 'southern claw' and 'northern claw' in Arabic.

name: Capricornus
visual_anchor: A faint delta-shaped arrowhead constellation depicting a mythological creature with the head of a goat and the tail of a fish.
core_traits: Zodiac constellation located in the southern sky between Sagittarius and Aquarius
Represents the mythical Sea-Goat, a hybrid creature with the upper body of a goat and the tail of a fish
Smallest constellation in the zodiac after Scorpius, easily traced as a triangular arrowhead
Gave its name to the Tropic of Capricorn in Earth's southern hemisphere

facts_and_myths.claim: The Tropic of Capricorn is named after this constellation because the winter solstice sun once occurred here.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In classical antiquity, the winter solstice occurred when the Sun was in Capricornus, though precession has since shifted it into Sagittarius.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Neptune was discovered in the constellation Capricornus on September 23, 1846, near the star Deneb Algedi.

facts_and_myths.claim: Capricornus is a star cluster that exploded in 2012.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is an ancient constellation whose stars have been stable and cataloged since ancient Babylonian times.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Greek mythology, the god Pan turned his lower half into a fish while jumping into the Nile to escape the monster Typhon.

name: Fomalhaut
visual_anchor: A lonely white star shining brightly in a dark empty southern sky, surrounded by a razor-sharp ring of cometary debris.
core_traits: Brightest star in the constellation Piscis Austrinus (The Southern Fish) and 18th-brightest star in the sky
Located approximately 25 light-years from Earth, shining with about 16 times the luminosity of our Sun
Surrounded by an prominent ring of cold debris dust resembling the 'Eye of Sauron'
One of the four 'Royal Stars' of ancient Persian astronomy, guarding the southern sky

facts_and_myths.claim: Hubble photographs of Fomalhaut's debris ring made it look so much like the 'Eye of Sauron' that the nickname became world-famous.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The sharp, tilted oval dust ring with the bright star offset in the center bears an uncanny resemblance to the fiery eye from Lord of the Rings.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In 2023, the James Webb Space Telescope discovered Fomalhaut has three nested asteroid belts, more complex than our own solar system.

facts_and_myths.claim: Fomalhaut is located inside our solar system between Mars and Jupiter.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Fomalhaut is an independent star located 25 light-years away in interstellar space.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name Fomalhaut comes from the Arabic 'Fam al-Hut', meaning 'mouth of the southern fish'.

name: Regulus
visual_anchor: A brilliant blue-white jewel star pulsating at the base of the sickle at the heart of Leo the Lion.
core_traits: Brightest star in the constellation Leo and 21st-brightest star in the entire night sky
Located roughly 79 light-years from Earth, sitting almost directly on the ecliptic path
Spins at a blistering speed of 320 km/s, completing a full rotation in just 15.9 hours and bulging heavily at the equator
Regularly occulted by the Moon and occasionally by planets like Venus and Mercury

facts_and_myths.claim: Regulus spins so fast that if it spun just 10% faster, centrifugal force would tear the star apart.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its rotational speed is 86% of the critical breakup velocity, squashing it into an oblate pumpkin shape.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name Regulus was given by Nicolaus Copernicus, translating from Latin as 'prince' or 'little king'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Regulus is a dead black hole with zero light output.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Regulus is a blazing four-star quadruple system dominated by a blue-white subgiant star 288 times more luminous than our Sun.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Because it lies right on the ecliptic, asteroid occultations of Regulus allow astronomers to measure asteroid profiles precisely.

name: Barnard's Star
visual_anchor: A small, ancient dim red dwarf star streaking across the background star field of Ophiuchus faster than any other star.
core_traits: Very low-mass red dwarf star in the constellation Ophiuchus, located about 5.96 light-years from Earth
Fourth-closest known individual star to the Sun after the three stars of the Alpha Centauri system
Holds the record for the highest proper motion of any known star, moving 10.3 arcseconds per year across the sky
Discovered in 1916 by American astronomer E. E. Barnard

facts_and_myths.claim: Barnard's Star moves across Earth's sky so fast that its motion can be spotted in photographs taken just a few years apart.
facts_and_myths.explanation: At 10.3 arcseconds per year, it travels the diameter of the full Moon in roughly 180 years, faster than any other star.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Around the year 11,800 AD, Barnard's Star will approach within 3.75 light-years of our Sun, temporarily becoming our closest star.

facts_and_myths.claim: Barnard's Star is a supermassive giant that shines brighter than the full Moon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is a dim red dwarf with only 14% of the Sun's mass and magnitude 9.5, completely invisible to the naked eye.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Project Daedalus in the 1970s was a British Interplanetary Society design study for an uncrewed nuclear fusion starship to explore Barnard's Star.

name: Summer Triangle
visual_anchor: A massive overhead triangle of three blazing white stars spanning the northern summer sky across the Milky Way band.
core_traits: Prominent astronomical asterism formed by three bright stars in three separate constellations: Vega (Lyra), Deneb (Cygnus), and Altair (Aquila)
Dominates the northern hemisphere sky during summer and autumn nights
Bisected down the middle by the glowing river of the Milky Way
Popularized as an educational navigational aid by British astronomer Patrick Moore in the 1950s

facts_and_myths.claim: The three stars of the Summer Triangle are located at almost the exact same distance from Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Altair is 17 light-years away, Vega is 25 light-years away, but Deneb is a colossal 2,600 light-years away; their triangle shape is purely a perspective alignment.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Deneb must be hundreds of thousands of times more luminous than Altair to appear almost as bright across that vast distance.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Summer Triangle is an official constellation recognized by the International Astronomical Union.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is an asterism connecting stars from three distinct official constellations: Lyra, Cygnus, and Aquila.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Japanese mythology, the Summer Triangle celebrates the romantic reunion of Orihime (Vega) and Hikoboshi (Altair) during Tanabata.

name: Orion's Belt
visual_anchor: Three brilliant blue-white supergiant stars aligned in a perfectly straight row across the celestial equator.
core_traits: Famous three-star asterism located at the waist of the constellation Orion
Composed of three massive, luminous blue supergiant stars: Alnitak, Alnilam, and Mintaka
Span less than 3 degrees of the sky in a remarkably straight line
Used as a primary navigational pointer: follow the belt southeast to Sirius, or northwest to Aldebaran and the Pleiades

facts_and_myths.claim: The stars of Orion's Belt can be used to easily locate both the brightest star in the sky and the Seven Sisters.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Drawing an imaginary line down to the left points directly to Sirius; extending it up to the right points to Aldebaran and the Pleiades.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Latin American tradition, the three stars are known as 'Las Tres Marias' (The Three Marys).

facts_and_myths.claim: All three stars in Orion's Belt are small rocky planets.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They are roaring blue supergiant stars tens of thousands of times more luminous and dozens of times more massive than our Sun.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Horsehead Nebula sits just beneath Alnitak, the easternmost star of the Belt.

name: Grand Canyon
visual_anchor: A vast, layered red-rock canyon carving through the Arizona plateau, plunging a mile deep under a golden sunset.
core_traits: Immense steep-sided gorge carved by the Colorado River in northwestern Arizona, USA
Spans 446 kilometers in length, up to 29 kilometers in width, and over 1,800 meters (1 mile) in depth
Exposes nearly two billion years of Earth's geological history across colorful rock strata
Recognized as one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World and a UNESCO World Heritage Site

facts_and_myths.claim: The Grand Canyon exposes rock layers dating back nearly two billion years, almost half the age of the Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Vishnu Basement Rocks exposed at the bottom of the canyon are roughly 1.84 billion years old.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Despite its immense depth, the Colorado River carved the modern canyon surprisingly quickly, over the last 5 to 6 million years.

facts_and_myths.claim: You can see dinosaur bones everywhere protruding from the walls of the Grand Canyon.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The rock layers are far older than the dinosaurs; only ancient marine fossils, trilobites, and plant imprints are found there.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Grand Canyon creates its own localized weather systems, with temperatures at the bottom often 15 degrees Celsius hotter than at the South Rim.

name: Great Barrier Reef
visual_anchor: A breathtaking aerial expanse of vibrant turquoise lagoons and kaleidoscope coral cays stretching along the Australian coast.
core_traits: World's largest coral reef system, composed of over 2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands
Stretches over 2,300 kilometers off the northeastern coast of Queensland, Australia
Largest single structure on Earth made by living organisms, clearly visible from outer space
Home to thousands of species of marine life, including sea turtles, sharks, clownfish, and rays

facts_and_myths.claim: The Great Barrier Reef is so vast that astronauts can see it with the naked eye from Earth orbit.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Covering an area of 344,400 square kilometers, its turquoise coral waters contrast clearly against the deep blue Pacific Ocean.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The reef undergoes a synchronized mass coral spawning event once a year, timed precisely to the lunar cycle in spring.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Great Barrier Reef is made entirely of dead mineral limestone rock with no living animals.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Corals are tiny living colonial invertebrate animals (polyps) that build calcium carbonate exoskeletons.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The reef is threatened by marine heatwaves causing coral bleaching, where corals expel their colorful symbiotic algae.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
visual_anchor: A snow-capped, flat-topped stratovolcano rising dramatically above the golden, acacia-dotted plains of the African savannah.
core_traits: Tallest mountain in Africa and the highest free-standing mountain in the world at 5,895 meters above sea level
Dormant stratovolcano located in northeastern Tanzania near the Kenyan border
Consists of three distinct volcanic cones: Kibo (highest), Mawenzi, and Shira
Climbers pass through five distinct ecological climate zones from tropical rainforest to arctic glaciers at the summit

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Kilimanjaro is a free-standing mountain that does not belong to any mountain range.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Unlike the Himalayas or Alps formed by plate collisions, Kilimanjaro was pushed up by volcanic rift activity as a solitary peak.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The glaciers on Kilimanjaro's summit have shrunk by over 80% since 1912 due to climate change.

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Kilimanjaro erupts with red-hot rivers of lava every summer.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The highest cone, Kibo, is dormant with its last major eruption occurring 360,000 years ago, although gas vents (fumaroles) still emit sulfur.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Virtually any physically fit hiker can reach the summit without technical mountaineering ropes or crampons.

name: Mount Fuji
visual_anchor: An iconic, perfectly symmetrical snow-capped volcanic cone framed against cherry blossoms and Lake Kawaguchi at sunrise.
core_traits: Highest mountain in Japan, standing at 3,776.24 meters on Honshu island
Active stratovolcano renowned for its exceptionally symmetrical conical shape
One of Japan's 'Three Holy Mountains' alongside Mount Tate and Mount Haku
Last erupted in December 1707 during the Hoei eruption, blanketing Edo (Tokyo) in volcanic ash

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Fuji is actually three separate volcanoes stacked on top of each other.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Geological history shows Komitake at the base, followed by Ko-Fuji (Old Fuji), and finally Shin-Fuji (New Fuji) at the top.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Over 300,000 people climb Mount Fuji every year, usually hiking through the night to witness the sunrise ('Goraiko') from the summit.

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Fuji is an extinct volcano that can never erupt again.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Mount Fuji is officially classified by volcanologists as an active volcano with a low eruption risk.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mount Fuji was registered as a UNESCO World Heritage cultural site in 2013 for inspiring centuries of Japanese art and literature.

name: Mount Vesuvius
visual_anchor: A menacing, twin-peaked volcano looming over the modern city of Naples and the ancient ruins of Pompeii in Italy.
core_traits: Somma-stratovolcano located on the Gulf of Naples in Campania, Italy
Infamous for its catastrophic eruption in 79 AD that buried the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum
Only volcano on the European mainland to have erupted within the last hundred years (last erupted in 1944)
Considered one of the most dangerous volcanoes in the world due to the 3 million people living in its blast shadow

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Vesuvius's 79 AD eruption buried Pompeii so thoroughly that the city remained hidden and preserved for over 1,500 years.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Deep pyroclastic flows and pumice preserved buildings, frescoes, and body hollows intact until rediscovery in the 18th century.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pliny the Younger's eyewitness letters describing the towering ash umbrella pine cloud gave birth to the term 'Plinian eruption'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Vesuvius has been completely extinct since ancient Roman times.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Vesuvius erupted repeatedly throughout history, including major eruptions in 1631, 1906, and during World War II in March 1944.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its volcanic soil is extraordinarily fertile, producing world-famous Lacryma Christi wine and sweet San Marzano tomatoes.

name: Mount St. Helens
visual_anchor: A gaping horseshoe-shaped crater mountain billowing steam in Washington State, surrounded by vast blowdown pine forests.
core_traits: Active stratovolcano located in Skamania County, Washington, in the Pacific Northwest region of the United States
Catastrophically erupted on May 18, 1980, following a massive 5.1 magnitude earthquake
The 1980 eruption triggered the largest subaerial landslide recorded in human history
Part of the Cascade Volcanic Arc, which forms an active segment of the Pacific Ring of Fire

facts_and_myths.claim: The 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens instantly removed 400 meters (1,300 feet) from the mountain's summit.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The catastrophic lateral blast blew off the entire north face and summit, reducing its elevation from 2,950 m to 2,549 m.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The blast shockwave flattened 600 square kilometers of prime Douglas fir forest in less than 3 minutes.

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount St. Helens erupted without any warning signs or tremors beforehand.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Thousands of earthquakes and a growing 100-meter bulge on the north flank gave scientists two months of advance warning.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A new volcanic lava dome has been steadily growing inside the crater ever since.

name: Mount Rainier
visual_anchor: A massive, heavily glaciated volcanic peak cloaked in white snow towering majestically over the skyline of Seattle, Washington.
core_traits: Highest mountain in Washington State and the Cascade Range, standing at 4,392 meters
Large active stratovolcano bearing more glacial ice than any other mountain in the contiguous United States
Ranked as one of the most dangerous volcanoes in the world due to the threat of catastrophic volcanic mudflows (lahars)
Revered by Pacific Northwest Indigenous tribes as Tahoma or Tacoma ('mother of waters')

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Rainier contains 25 major named glaciers covering over 90 square kilometers of ice.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Emmons Glacier and Carbon Glacier are the largest glaciers in the lower 48 US states.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: If Mount Rainier erupts, heat melting its vast glaciers could send massive lahars down river valleys into the Seattle-Tacoma suburbs within hours.

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Rainier is an extinct mountain that formed millions of years before the dinosaurs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Mount Rainier is a young volcano that began growing less than one million years ago and remains volcanically active.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Subterranean steam vents keep summit ice caves carved out beneath its snow-filled craters.

name: Denali
visual_anchor: A colossal, ice-clad granite massif rising dramatically 5,500 meters above the flat Alaskan tundra into freezing Arctic skies.
core_traits: Highest mountain peak in North America, with a summit elevation of 6,190 meters above sea level
Located in the Alaska Range inside Denali National Park and Preserve
Has the third highest topographic prominence in the world after Mount Everest and Aconcagua
Known for extreme sub-zero temperatures, savage jet-stream winds, and treacherous Arctic climbing conditions

facts_and_myths.claim: From base to peak, Denali is taller than Mount Everest.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Everest sits on the 4,200-meter Tibetan Plateau (base-to-peak rise of 4,600 m), while Denali rises 5,500 meters directly from a 600-meter plain.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The US government officially restored its indigenous Koyukon Athabascan name 'Denali' in 2015, dropping Mount McKinley.

facts_and_myths.claim: Denali was named after a famous Alaskan grizzly bear.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Denali comes from the Koyukon word 'Deenaalee', meaning 'the high one' or 'the tall one'.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Due to its high northern latitude (63 degreesN), atmospheric pressure at its summit feels equivalent to an elevation 700 meters higher in the Himalayas.

name: K2
visual_anchor: A terrifying, sheer-faced pyramid of dark rock and blue ice piercing storm clouds on the Pakistan-China border.
core_traits: Second-highest mountain in the world at 8,611 meters above sea level
Located in the Karakoram range spanning the border between Pakistan and China
Nicknamed 'The Savage Mountain' due to extreme technical climbing difficulty and high fatality rates
Features notorious hazards including the treacherous 'Bottleneck' serac couloir below the summit

facts_and_myths.claim: Historically, roughly one climber dies for every four who successfully reach the summit of K2.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With a historic fatality-to-summit ratio exceeding 20%, K2 is far more dangerous and technically demanding than Mount Everest.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: K2 was the last of the world's 14 eight-thousanders to be climbed in winter, conquered by a 10-man Nepali team in January 2021.

facts_and_myths.claim: K2 was named after a secret military spy submarine code.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The name K2 signifies the second peak surveyed in the Karakoram range by British surveyor T.G. Montgomerie in 1856.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Unlike Everest, K2 cannot be climbed using commercial guided tours by inexperienced mountaineers.

name: Matterhorn
visual_anchor: A breathtaking four-sided pyramidal horn of razor-sharp jagged rock and snow standing isolated in the Swiss Alps above Zermatt.
core_traits: Iconic pyramidal mountain peak in the Pennine Alps, straddling the border between Switzerland and Italy
Summit stands at 4,478 meters, with four steep faces pointing toward the four cardinal directions
First summitted in July 1865 by Edward Whymper's team, which ended in a tragic descent accident
Famous inspiration for the triangular shape of Toblerone Swiss chocolate bars

facts_and_myths.claim: The four steep triangular faces of the Matterhorn face the four cardinal compass points: north, south, east, and west.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Glacial erosion from multiple cirque glaciers carved the peak into an almost perfectly symmetrical pyramidal horn (glacial horn).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Matterhorn's summit is made of African continental plate rock that was pushed over the European plate during Alpine mountain building.

facts_and_myths.claim: The famous logo on Toblerone chocolate boxes was permanently removed because it violated Swissness laws.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When production moved partially to Slovakia in 2023, Toblerone had to replace the specific Matterhorn illustration with a generic mountain.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Over 500 climbers have lost their lives attempting the Matterhorn since 1865.

name: Yellowstone Supervolcano
visual_anchor: A massive steaming plateau caldera in Wyoming featuring bubbling multi-colored geothermal pools and surging geysers.
core_traits: Volcanic caldera and supervolcano in Yellowstone National Park in the western United States
Powered by a massive mantle hotspot under the North American tectonic plate
Caldera measures roughly 72 by 45 kilometers, formed by three cataclysmic super-eruptions over the last 2.1 million years
Drives the world's greatest concentration of geysers, hot springs, and mud pots

facts_and_myths.claim: A super-eruption of Yellowstone 631,000 years ago covered half of North America in a blanket of volcanic ash.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Lava Creek eruption ejected over 1,000 cubic kilometers of rock, ash, and pyroclastic debris.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Grand Prismatic Spring in Yellowstone is colored vivid orange and blue by heat-loving extremophile thermophilic bacteria.

facts_and_myths.claim: Yellowstone is 'overdue' for an eruption and will blow up any day now.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Volcanoes do not follow precise schedules; the US Geological Survey monitors it constantly and rates the annual eruption probability at 1 in 730,000.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Yellowstone was established in 1872 as the world's first national park.

name: Old Faithful Geyser
visual_anchor: A towering column of boiling water and billowing white steam erupting 40 meters into the blue sky above a steaming sinter mound.
core_traits: World-famous cone geyser located in Yellowstone National Park's Upper Geyser Basin in Wyoming, USA
Renowned for its remarkable predictability, erupting roughly every 60 to 90 minutes
Blasts thousands of gallons of boiling water to heights between 30 and 55 meters
Named in 1870 by the Washburn-Langford-Doane Expedition because of its reliable eruptions

facts_and_myths.claim: Old Faithful erupts with clockwork regularity exactly on the hour, every hour, on the minute.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its eruption intervals fluctuate between 60 and 110 minutes depending on the volume and duration of the previous blast.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A single eruption expels between 14,000 and 32,000 liters of boiling water in just a few minutes.

facts_and_myths.claim: Early explorers and soldiers in Yellowstone used Old Faithful as a natural laundry machine.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Soldiers discovered placing dirty woolen clothes in the geyser vent washed them clean during the next eruption without damaging the fabric.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Water temperature inside the geyser's plumbing reaches over 129 degrees Celsius before flashing into explosive steam.

name: Victoria Falls
visual_anchor: A colossal sheet of roaring white water plunging 108 meters into a narrow basalt gorge, sending spray clouds miles into the sky.
core_traits: Spectacular waterfall on the Zambezi River on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe in southern Africa
Classified as the largest waterfall in the world based on combined width (1,708 m) and height (108 m)
Known locally in the Lozi language as Mosi-oa-Tunya ('The Smoke That Thunders')
Produces a towering spray mist that can be seen from over 50 kilometers away

facts_and_myths.claim: During low-water season, daredevils can swim right up to the cliff edge in the natural 'Devil's Pool'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A natural rock lip prevents swimmers from being swept over the 100-meter abyss when river flow is at its annual low.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: David Livingstone was the first European to view the falls in 1855, naming them in honor of Queen Victoria.

facts_and_myths.claim: Victoria Falls is the tallest continuous vertical drop waterfall on Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the world's tallest waterfall at 979 meters; Victoria Falls is the largest sheet of falling water.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The spray from the falls supports a unique localized rainforest sustained entirely by artificial mist.

name: Niagara Falls
visual_anchor: A thundering turquoise curtain of churning water plunging into billowing mist, straddling the US-Canada border.
core_traits: Group of three waterfalls spanning the international border between Ontario, Canada, and New York State, USA
Composed of the Horseshoe Falls (largest), the American Falls, and the Bridal Veil Falls
Has the highest flow rate of any waterfall in North America, with over 168,000 cubic meters of water per minute
Major tourist attraction and crucial source of hydroelectric power for the region

facts_and_myths.claim: In 1901, 63-year-old schoolteacher Annie Edson Taylor became the first person to survive going over Niagara Falls in a barrel.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Taylor strapped herself into an airtight wooden pickle barrel and plunged over the 51-meter Horseshoe Falls, surviving with minor cuts.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Up to 75% of the water flowing toward Niagara Falls is diverted through tunnels into massive hydroelectric turbines.

facts_and_myths.claim: Niagara Falls froze into a solid, motionless block of solid ice in 2014.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Extreme winter freezes create a thick surface ice crust and frozen spray, but water continues flowing vigorously underneath.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Erosion from the rushing water causes the falls to retreat upstream by roughly one foot every year.

name: Iguazu Falls
visual_anchor: A sprawling horseshoe staircase of 275 thunderous waterfalls cascading through lush subtropical jungle mist on the Argentina-Brazil border.
core_traits: Massive chain of 275 individual waterfalls along the Iguazu River on the border of Argentina and Brazil
Spans nearly 2.7 kilometers in width, dropping between 60 and 82 meters into misty rainforest chasms
Anchored by the 'Devil's Throat' (Garganta del Diablo), a dramatic U-shaped chasm where half the river's flow plunges
Surrounded by UNESCO World Heritage subtropical rainforest national parks teeming with toucans and jaguars

facts_and_myths.claim: When US First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt saw Iguazu Falls, she famously exclaimed: 'Poor Niagara!'
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its sheer scale, lush jungle setting, and 275 individual cascades make it wider and more visually dramatic than Niagara.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In Guarani indigenous myth, the falls were created when a jealous serpent god sliced the riverbed in rage after a lover fled.

facts_and_myths.claim: Iguazu Falls is located high in the snow-covered Andes Mountains.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is located in the warm, humid Atlantic subtropical rainforest shared by Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Over 80% of the falls lie on the Argentine side, but the most panoramic viewpoint is from the Brazilian side.

name: Angel Falls
visual_anchor: A breathtaking, ribbon-like cascade of water plunging nearly a kilometer off a sheer tabletop mountain in the Venezuelan jungle.
core_traits: World's highest uninterrupted waterfall, with a total height of 979 meters and a free plunge of 807 meters
Plunges from the edge of the Auyan-tepui tabletop mountain in Canaima National Park, Venezuela
Known in the indigenous Pemon language as Kerepakupai Meru ('waterfall of the deepest place')
The waterfall is so high that during dry months, water atomizes into fine mist before reaching the bottom

facts_and_myths.claim: Angel Falls was named after angels sent from heaven in religious folklore.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It was named after Jimmie Angel, an American aviator who crash-landed his monoplane near the summit in 1937 while searching for gold.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Jimmie Angel and his crew had to hike for 11 grueling days down the tepui to reach civilization.

facts_and_myths.claim: The waterfall served as the visual inspiration for 'Paradise Falls' in Pixar's animated movie 'Up'.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Pixar animators spent weeks camping on Venezuelan tepuis sketching Angel Falls to design the movie's setting.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Tepuis are ancient sandstone tabletop mesas dating back nearly two billion years to the Precambrian era.

name: Yosemite Falls
visual_anchor: A majestic three-tiered ribbon of glacial meltwater cascading down a sheer granite cliff in Yosemite National Park, California.
core_traits: Highest waterfall in Yosemite National Park and fifth-highest in North America, dropping a total of 739 meters
Consists of three distinct sections: Upper Yosemite Fall, Middle Cascades, and Lower Yosemite Fall
Powered almost entirely by snowmelt from the Sierra Nevada mountains
Peak flow occurs in late spring (May and June), frequently slowing to a mere trickle by late summer

facts_and_myths.claim: Yosemite Falls can produce an ice cone at its base during winter that reaches over 30 stories high.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Freezing spray builds an enormous hollow cone of snow and ice up to 90 meters tall beneath the Upper Fall.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: During clear full moons in spring, the mist from Lower Yosemite Fall frequently creates glowing lunar rainbows ('moonbows').

facts_and_myths.claim: Yosemite Falls flows continuously at maximum volume 365 days a year without changing.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because it relies on winter snowpack melt, the falls often dry up completely by August or September until autumn rains begin.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The indigenous Ahwahneechee people believed the pool at the bottom was inhabited by the spirits of witches and Poloti wind spirits.

name: Amazon River
visual_anchor: A colossal, muddy serpent river winding through dense emerald tropical canopy, spanning miles wide under tropical storm clouds.
core_traits: Largest river in the world by water discharge volume, carrying more water than the next seven largest rivers combined
Accounts for roughly 20% of the entire planet's freshwater river flow into the world's oceans
Flows over 6,400 kilometers from the Peruvian Andes through Brazil into the Atlantic Ocean
Has zero bridges crossing its entire main stem due to its immense width and dense surrounding rainforest

facts_and_myths.claim: There is not a single bridge crossing anywhere along the entire main stem of the Amazon River.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because it flows through sparsely populated tropical rainforest where boats are standard, building bridges is economically and logistically unnecessary.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The fresh water discharged by the Amazon freshens the Atlantic Ocean for over 150 kilometers offshore.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Amazon River was named by Spanish conquistadors after warrior women they encountered in battle.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Francisco de Orellana named the river after battling fierce female Indigenous warriors reminiscent of Greek mythological Amazons.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A subterranean twin river named the Hamza River flows 4,000 meters beneath the Amazon.

name: Nile River
visual_anchor: A radiant blue river cutting a lush green ribbon of fertility through the arid, golden desert sands of Egypt.
core_traits: Historically recognized as the longest river in the world, flowing approximately 6,650 kilometers northward across northeastern Africa
Formed by two major tributaries: the White Nile (originating in Lake Victoria) and the Blue Nile (originating in Lake Tana, Ethiopia)
Cradle of ancient Egyptian civilization, providing silt, water, and transport across thousands of years
Empties into the Mediterranean Sea via a vast triangular river delta

facts_and_myths.claim: The ancient Egyptian calendar was built entirely around the three seasons of the Nile River.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The seasons were Akhet (inundation/flooding), Peret (planting/growth), and Shemu (harvest/dry season).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Nearly 95% of Egypt's modern population lives within a few kilometers of the Nile's banks.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Nile River flows backwards from north to south toward the equator.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Nile flows northward from higher elevation highlands in Central Africa down to sea level at the Mediterranean Sea.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Blue Nile provides over 80% of the river's water and fertile silt during the summer flood stage.

name: Mississippi River
visual_anchor: A broad, curving brown river carrying paddle steamers and barge tows through the heartland plains of North America.
core_traits: Chief river of the second-largest drainage system in North America, flowing 3,766 kilometers south to the Gulf of Mexico
Rises from its modest glacial source at Lake Itasca in northern Minnesota
Together with its Missouri tributary, forms the fourth-longest river system on Earth
Celebrated in American literature, music, and folklore, most famously by Mark Twain in 'Life on the Mississippi'

facts_and_myths.claim: A drop of water falling into Lake Itasca takes about 90 days to travel the entire length of the Mississippi to the Gulf of Mexico.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Flowing at an average speed of 2 to 3 miles per hour, water takes three months to complete the 2,340-mile journey.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The river's name comes from the Ojibwe word 'Misi-ziibi', meaning 'Great River'.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Mississippi River flows faster than any waterfall on Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Mississippi is a slow, meandering low-gradient river, dropping only about 450 meters over its entire 3,700-kilometer length.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: During the catastrophic 1811-1812 New Madrid earthquakes, ground uplift caused parts of the river to temporarily flow backward.

name: Yangtze River
visual_anchor: A mighty Asian river carving through the towering misty limestone gorges of the Three Gorges into China's fertile plains.
core_traits: Longest river in Asia and the third-longest river on Earth, stretching 6,300 kilometers across China
Flows entirely within one single country, originating on the Tibetan Plateau and emptying into the East China Sea at Shanghai
Home to the Three Gorges Dam, the world's largest hydroelectric power station
River basin is home to nearly one-third of the entire population of China

facts_and_myths.claim: The Three Gorges Dam on the Yangtze River holds so much water that it measurably slowed the rotation of the Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: NASA geophysicists calculated that raising 39 trillion kilograms of water 175 meters above sea level increased Earth's moment of inertia, slowing its rotation by 0.06 microseconds.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Yangtze was historically home to the Baiji (Yangtze river dolphin), declared functionally extinct in 2006.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Yangtze River is identical to the Yellow River.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They are two distinct river systems; the Yellow River (Huang He) lies to the north, while the Yangtze (Chang Jiang) flows through central and southern China.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Yangtze basin produces roughly 70% of China's rice harvest.

name: Danube River
visual_anchor: A majestic European river sweeping past grand historical castles, gothic cathedrals, and illuminated bridges in Budapest and Vienna.
core_traits: Second-longest river in Europe, flowing 2,850 kilometers eastward from Germany's Black Forest to the Black Sea
Flows through or touches more countries than any other river on Earth (10 sovereign nations)
Passes through four European capital cities: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, and Belgrade
Immortalized by Austrian composer Johann Strauss II in his famous waltz 'The Blue Danube'

facts_and_myths.claim: The Danube River touches or flows through ten different countries, a world record.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It borders or traverses Germany, Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria, Moldova, and Ukraine.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Danube Delta is the second largest and best-preserved river delta in Europe, hosting over 300 bird species.

facts_and_myths.claim: The water of the Danube River is naturally vivid royal blue like swimming pool water.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its waters are typical river greenish-brown; the 'Blue Danube' moniker came from Johann Strauss's romantic musical waltz.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Parts of the Danube near Immendingen sink completely underground through limestone caves, emerging 12 kilometers away into the Rhine basin.

name: Ganges River
visual_anchor: A sacred golden river at dusk lined with ancient stone ghats, flickering oil lamps, and bathing pilgrims in Varanasi, India.
core_traits: Sacred transboundary river flowing 2,525 kilometers across India and Bangladesh to the Bay of Bengal
Revered by over a billion Hindus as the living personification of the goddess Ganga
Rises from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas as the Bhagirathi River
Combines with the Brahmaputra to form the Sundarbans Delta, the world's largest river delta

facts_and_myths.claim: The Ganges delta hosts the Sundarbans, the largest contiguous mangrove forest on Earth and home to swimming Bengal tigers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The mangrove delta spans 10,000 square kilometers across India and Bangladesh, providing sanctuary for endangered royal Bengal tigers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Hindus believe bathing in the holy waters of the Ganges cleanses a person of sins and frees them from the cycle of reincarnation.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Ganges River is completely dry for 11 months of the year.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Ganges is a perennial river fed continuously by Himalayan glacial melt and intense annual monsoon rains.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Ganges is home to the endangered freshwater Ganges river dolphin, which is functionally blind and navigates entirely using echolocation.

name: Colorado River
visual_anchor: An emerald and rust-red river cutting dramatic Horseshoe Bend meanders through sheer sandstone canyons in the American Southwest.
core_traits: Major river of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico, flowing 2,330 kilometers
World-famous as the principal geological architect that carved the Grand Canyon over millions of years
Impounded by colossal engineering marvels including the Hoover Dam and Glen Canyon Dam
Lifeline providing drinking water and irrigation to over 40 million people across seven US states

facts_and_myths.claim: Because of heavy agricultural and municipal water diversions, the Colorado River rarely reaches the sea.
facts_and_myths.explanation: So much water is drawn out for cities and farms that its delta in Mexico's Gulf of California has been largely desiccated sand since the 1960s.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The river's name comes from Spanish for 'colored reddish', describing the heavy reddish silt it traditionally transported.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Colorado River was artificially dug by US military excavators in the 1930s.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Colorado is a natural ancient river system that began carving the Colorado Plateau millions of years ago.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: John Wesley Powell led the historic first recorded boat expedition down the Colorado River through the Grand Canyon in 1869.

name: Mariana Trench
visual_anchor: A deep oceanic abyss plunging into total Stygian darkness under crushing hydrostatic pressures, illuminated by a research submarine beam.
core_traits: Deepest oceanic trench on Earth, located in the western Pacific Ocean east of the Mariana Islands
Reaches its maximum depth at the Challenger Deep, measured at nearly 11,000 meters (36,000 feet) below sea level
Plunges deeper below sea level than Mount Everest rises above it
Subject to crushing hydrostatic pressure exceeding 1,000 atmospheres (over 8 tons per square inch)

facts_and_myths.claim: If Mount Everest were dropped into the Challenger Deep, its summit would still be submerged under more than 2 kilometers of water.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Everest stands 8,848 meters tall, while Challenger Deep is roughly 10,994 meters deep, leaving 2,146 meters of water above its peak.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Film director James Cameron made the first solo descent to Challenger Deep in 2012 in the Deepsea Challenger submersible.

facts_and_myths.claim: Because of the immense pressure, the bottom of the Mariana Trench is completely devoid of all biological life.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Scientists discovered thriving extremophile ecosystems including snailfish, amphipods, xenophyophores, and microbial mats.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Swiss oceanographer Jacques Piccard and US Navy Lieutenant Don Walsh made the historic first dive in bathyscaphe Trieste in 1960.

name: Dead Sea
visual_anchor: A shimmering cobalt hypersaline lake bordered by glistening white salt crystal pillars under the desert sun between Jordan and Israel.
core_traits: Hypersaline terminal lake bordered by Jordan to the east and Israel and the West Bank to the west
Its shores and water surface are the lowest land elevation on Earth, over 430 meters below sea level
Water is roughly 9.6 times saltier than the ocean, with a salinity around 34%
Extreme density allows humans to float effortlessly on the surface without treading water

facts_and_myths.claim: A person cannot naturally sink in the Dead Sea even if they try.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its water density (1.24 kg/L) makes the human body so buoyant that it bobs like a cork on the surface.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Dead Sea is landlocked with no outlets; incoming water from the Jordan River can only leave through evaporation, leaving behind thick salt deposits.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Dead Sea is a freshwater lake filled with trout and dolphins.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its extreme salt and mineral concentrations make multicellular plant and animal life impossible, giving it the name 'Dead Sea'.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Cleopatra was said to love the Dead Sea's mineral-rich black mud, using it as an ancient cosmetic spa treatment.

name: Great Salt Lake
visual_anchor: A wide, shallow inland salt lake reflecting dramatic purple mountains and shimmering pink-tinted waters in northern Utah.
core_traits: Largest saltwater lake in the Western Hemisphere, located in the northern part of Utah, USA
Endorheic lake with no outlet to the sea, where minerals accumulate as water evaporates
Remnant of ancient prehistoric Lake Bonneville, which covered much of western Utah during the Ice Age
Supports massive populations of brine shrimp and millions of migrating native and migratory shorebirds

facts_and_myths.claim: The northern half of the Great Salt Lake is bright pink while the southern half is blue-green.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A railroad causeway divided the lake in 1959; the hypersaline northern arm bloomed with salt-loving pink bacteria and algae (halophiles).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Bonneville Salt Flats to the west host world land speed record attempts on their glass-smooth salt crust.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Great Salt Lake is home to schools of great white sharks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: No fish can survive in its hypersaline water; its animal life consists of brine shrimp and brine flies.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Robert Smithson constructed his famous land art installation 'Spiral Jetty' on the lake's northeastern shore in 1970.

name: Lake Baikal
visual_anchor: A vast Siberian lake of crystal-clear turquoise glass ice revealing frozen methane bubbles trapped under winter frost.
core_traits: World's oldest and deepest freshwater lake, situated in mountainous southern Siberia, Russia
Reaches an extraordinary maximum depth of 1,642 meters (over 5,300 feet)
Contains roughly 22% to 23% of the world's entire surface liquid freshwater, more than all five North American Great Lakes combined
Over 25 million years old, hosting over 1,000 endemic species found nowhere else on Earth (including the nerpa seal)

facts_and_myths.claim: Lake Baikal contains more freshwater than all five of the North American Great Lakes combined.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Despite covering less surface area than Lake Superior, its extreme depth gives it a volume of 23,615 cubic kilometers of water.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It is the only lake on Earth home to a purely freshwater seal species, the adorable round Baikal seal (nerpa).

facts_and_myths.claim: Lake Baikal freezes so solidly in winter that trains and trucks can drive across its surface.
